articles.title: Bosses - The Witcher 3 Guide - IGN
articles.summary: There are many powerful monsters to fight during a playthrough of The Witcher 3 - from the various monsters that can be hunted in Witcher Contracts, creatures
articles.body:
There are many powerful monsters to fight during a playthrough of The Witcher 3 - from the various monsters that can be hunted in Witcher Contracts , creatures and humans found in the various Side Quests and of course the immensely powerful warriors of the Wild Hunt. This page goes over the various boss fights you will find in the main story and provide some tips to gain the upper hand.

The Royal Griffon is your tutorial at being a Witcher. You go through the motions of your first hunt and are tested with a flying foe that is terrorizing the local region.

Use Aard, or the Crossbow to get him grounded while he tries to swoop.

Caleb Menge is the leader of the Witch Hunters in Novigrad and you have the opportunity to fight him while you are infiltrating the Witch Hunter's garrison for information on Dandelion in Count Reuvan's Treasure .

He is a human and can be knocked over and executed.

Hanged Man's Oil will aid you in fighting all of the Witch Hunters as well as Menge.

Maintaining your cover and letting Triss get tortured results in Triss killing him in a cut scene.

The Crone fight is a 3-on-1 playing as Ciri, which almost makes it a fair fight. They don't have a large swath of attacks to choose from but they will use their numbers against you and jump around a lot. The struggle of this fight is that you are outnumbered with no heals. Dodge around after a few attacks before making distance. Don't fight them in groups try and stick to the one that is alone.

Brewess - She is a melee fighter and will swing her arms in front of her for multiple hit attacks to stun lock you. She has the most health and will try to get close to you. Focus her down before the other more slippery targets.

Weavess and Whispess - These two will typically run away or try to stay on the sides. Engaging them will often result in the teleporting away one way or another. To close the gaps, hold the heavy attack button while full stamina to charge forward in a line at your lock on target.

They can send glowing boiling blood out from under them that travels to you. Avoid standing on it or you will get poisoned. There is a similar attack where they dive under the blood and pop out, it looks similar but does not glow.

They also send out a wave of ravens that harms you if you touch it when they teleport away. They will also throw limbs and bones at you from the sidelines as a ranged attack so stay on your guard.

There are several times throughout the main story questline that Geralt (or Ciri ) will face off against the captains of the Wild Hunt. There's the soldier Nithral , the hulking Imlerith , the mage-like navigator Caranthir and finally the King of the Wild Hunt himself, Eredin .

Here are some basic tips to taking on each boss - be sure to check out their individual pages for full strategies.

Nithral is the first Wild Hunt warrior that Geralt faces, deep in the elven ruins during the quest Wandering in the Dark with Kiera Metz. He swaps between melee attacks with his axe and a protective bubble he heals in until you finish off the Hounds he summons.

Let Keira Help - Thankfully, our hero is aided by the sorceress Keira Metz during this fight, who will use electric attacks to shock and stun your opponent giving you a lot of openings.

Use Signs- Nithral's attacks are powerful, yet he's not particularly quick - use Yrden to slow him down and Quen to protect yourself from his devastating attacks.

Witcher Tools - Bombs, Oils, and Potions are helpful for boss fights. You may not have a ton at this point in the game but make sure you use what you do have for the advantage they grant. These are tools every Witcher should be acclimated to preparing ahead of fights.

Focus on the Hounds - Each time you manage to take away 1/3 of his health bar, Nithral will teleport to the center of the arena and shield himself while summoning Hounds to aid him. Focus your attacks on taking out these foes as quickly as possible, since Nithral will regain HP while his shield is up and it lasts as long as there are Hounds in the field. He may heal to full but his health can easily be lost all over again.

Imlerith is the second member of the elite Wild Hunt soldiers that Geralt faces in single combat, during the mid-game mission Bald Mountain . This is the first of the Wild Hunt captains to utilize their Frost Shield ability - though certainly not the last.

Use Igni - Geralt can strip the frozen shield away with this sign. Doing this allows him to deal far greater damage - though the shield will re-appear whenever Imlerith teleports around the arena.

Imlerith is slow - His shield-and-giant-mace combat make him a formidable opponent, since he can block any attacks from the front (unless he is stunned). Thankfully, his size makes him slower than most opponents, so use this to your advantage and place a Yrden trap to get around behind him.

Use Bombs - Imlerith is also vulnerable to Grapeshot and Samum bombs. Grapeshot will blast away his Frost Shield and Samum will blind / stun him, allowing you to get in some quick and heavy attacks.

At the end of the game, during the second-to-last mission On Thin Ice , Geralt and friends will face off against two high-ranking members of the Wild Hunt. The first is their navigator and mage, Caranthir .

You start this fight as Ciri in Rage Mode. Use your mobility to avoid his attacks as he tries to teleport next to you and decimate as much of his HP as possible before triggering a cutscene once he loses about a 1/3rd of his HP.

As Geralt: Geralt will have a tougher time dealing with Caranthir than Ciri did. The mage will fire blasts of icy magic at the Witcher, which deals damage and slows your attack speed.

Roll Closer - Caranthir doesn't directly attack Geralt, preferring instead to attack with magic from a distance while teleporting around. Use dodge/roll to simultaneously avoid his ice blasts and close the distance between you, then follow your evasions up with a blast of Igni to eliminate his frost armor followed by strikes with your sword.

Ice Elemental Opening - Caranthir will perform a lengthy spell that summons an Ice Elemental. While he's busy performing the spell, use this time to launch an offensive. Elemental Cover - Once the summoning spell is complete, the elemental will march slowly towards Geralt. Use this to your advantage and try to position the Golem between you and Caranthir. The sorcerer will keep casting ice spells, but you can use the Elemental creature as cover. These spells also damage the golem, which will kill it far quicker than hitting it with a sword.

Elemental Cover - Once the summoning spell is complete, the elemental will march slowly towards Geralt. Use this to your advantage and try to position the Golem between you and Caranthir. The sorcerer will keep casting ice spells, but you can use the Elemental creature as cover. These spells also damage the golem, which will kill it far quicker than hitting it with a sword.

At the end of On Thin Ice , Geralt finally confronts the King of the Wild Hunt. This is a tough and lengthy boss fight, but is easily survivable if the Witcher knows his foe.

Dodge, Sign, Dodge, Attack - Eredin's battle strategy at the onset of this fight is very similar to Imlerith's, in that he attacks with a combo, then teleports to gain a better angle and attacks again. The big difference is that Eredin is much faster than Imlerith, so be sure to have perfected your dodging skills or have a bunch of restorative potions on hand. Dodge his first attack and blast him with Igni to dispell his Frost Shield , then dodge his counterattack and strike with your sword.

Roll your heart out - Once Eredin pulls Geralt off of the ship to the fields, continue avoiding his attacks and countering. Eventually the KotWH will teleport to a safe distance and begin summoning icy meteors to rain down upon Geralt. Use the roll evasion to avoid being crushed, and make your way towards Eredin. If you move quickly enough (you can also just sprint at him), you'll avoid the falling ice and be able to score some damage while he casts his spell.

Avoid the Nodes - The same principle can be applied to Eredin's other magic attack, which spawn on Geralt and trigger icy shockwaves when they detonate. Continuously roll away from the blast and close with your opponent to deal damage or take out his shield with Igni. Repeat this until the King teleports back to the ship, then sword-slap him once more to end the fight.

While Hearts of Stone is a relatively small expansion, it still introduces new characters, and enemies, which will have you fighting powerful new enemies.

The Toad Prince is a surprisingly tough battle given you're unwittingly thrown into it - during the first main quest in the expansion, no less. However, this boss battle can be made easier if you keep a few things in mind:

It deals poison damage , so dodge to avoid its attacks or use Quen to nullify them. You can also use Golden Oriole potion to turn poison damage into healing. You can find this recipe as a random drop in containers, or purchase it from the merchant in the Herbalist's Hut northeast of Oxenfurt.

You can also use Golden Oriole potion to turn poison damage into healing. You can find this recipe as a random drop in containers, or purchase it from the merchant in the Herbalist's Hut northeast of Oxenfurt.

Try to stick to the sides of the toad to make it easier to avoid its frontal attacks.

It's vulnerable to fire damage (Igni or bombs), as well as Cursed Oil.

This means your best offense is going to be a combination of either the Igni sign or explosive bombs depending on how strong your magic is, while hacking away with your sword. Northern Wind, Grapeshot, and Dragon's Dream work well, but the best bomb to equip for this battle is Dancing Star since its wide, fiery blast radius will help set the beast alight better than any of the others.

Between fire blasts, use Yrden whenever possible to capitalize on its weakness, and if you need to slow the rampaging toad, try using the Northern Wind bombs to slow it considerably.

Once you do away with roughly 90-95% of the monster's health, a cutscene will trigger, and the battle will end.

To defeat the Ofieri mage, the best course of action is to first defeat his entourage. Use your dodge/roll to avoid the mage's magic attacks - if you're lucky, some of his henchmen will get caught in them - and deal with the soldiers as they advance on you.

Once his guards have been taken care of, the Mage is fairly simple to get rid of. He can teleport and fling sand at you, which you can easily dodge, but he can also turn into a tornado and chase you. When this happens, just run away until the attack ends - it will one-hit you if you're not wearing armour.

His biggest weakness is Axii, especially if you're using an upgraded version, or Aard - though Aard can be tricky because you need to close distance on him before he recovers from the stun attack. Luckily, he doesn't have much health, so he'll be dead with a few swings of your sword.

While the Sand Mage has almost nothing worth taking on his body, there is a chest on the beach to the south, near the shipwreck, which can contain some random gear.

Preparation: The Caretaker is a Relict, thus weak to Relict Oil, so you should apply some to your sword before the fight, especially if you're underleveled (the quest is recommended level 35.)

The Caretaker is a formidable opponent, primarily because any of his attacks that successfully land will regenerate a large portion of his health . The best strategy for efficiently defeating this boss is to constantly retreat down the long pathways in the garden, then avoid his special attack and rush in to deal damage. Quen can also be used to mitigate his healing abilities .

His special attacks come in three phases (in addition to his basic swipe attacks), which advance when you deplete his health past the dividing lines in his life bar:

Phase One: The Caretaker sends a wave of energy towards his opponent. This is indicated by the large blue-green cone that appears on the ground in front of him a few seconds before his attack. Use a backwards dodge or roll to avoid taking damage, then roll towards him and execute an attack combo while he wrenches his shovel from the ground.

After (roughly) five seconds, the Caretaker will recover and another energy circle will appear on the ground around him. Dodge backwards (no need to roll - the circle isn't wide enough to merit that) to avoid taking damage in the circle and regenerating your enemy's health, then wait for him to execute his energy wave attack once more.

Ghostbuster: Each time you reach the next phase of this fight, the Caretaker will summon a group of specters to use as fodder to regenerate his health. Kill as many of these ghosts as you can (while avoiding the Caretaker) in order to prevent him from regenerating his entire life bar.

Phase Two: Instead of the energy wave, the Caretaker will channel his power into the blade of his shovel and charge at you. The best way to avoid this is to perform a roll towards him, avoiding the charge either to the left or to the right.

After avoiding the attack, sweep back in to deal damage while he recovers, then avoid his rejuvenation circle and await another charge.

Phase Three: After depleting two-thirds of his health, the Caretaker will begin using both his charge attack and his energy wave. Keep a close watchful eye on his movements to predict what the attack will be, and continue avoiding them and attacking while he recovers until the fight is done.

Preparation: The Wraith from the Painting is a specter, so it's weak to Specter Oil and Yrden. You should apply this oil to your sword before the fight.

After moving through the door into the hall, you'll have a short boss fight with a very angry wraith.

If her health gets low, she'll activate a healing portal in one of the four paintings along the walls - it glows bright green. Strike these with your sword (quite awkward to do) or a destructive sign like Igni to prevent her from healing or using them to teleport around the arena.

Generally, you've got enough time to jog over there, which is important to note because running will consume stamina also used to cast signs. With the portal dealt with, continue to attack the wraith.

You should also use Quen to prevent yourself from taking too much damage (she has lengthy combos and a long range lunge), and Yrden to slow or deal additional damage, as you would any other spirit.

Completionists: You can earn the When It's Many Against One achievement if you fight all six phantom Olgierds at once. The general tips below will still apply, but you will also want to get the Rend and Whirlwind sword skills for additional damage and utility.

When the battle begins, you're surrounded by six phantoms. Here are some tips that will help throughout the fight:

Unless you attack them first, the phantoms will only awaken one at a time, so avoid taking on multiple at once. However, area-of-effect damage, such as Aard, Igni, an Yrden trap, or even Quen with the shield burst upgrade, can unintentionally trigger surrounding enemies.

However, area-of-effect damage, such as Aard, Igni, an Yrden trap, or even Quen with the shield burst upgrade, can unintentionally trigger surrounding enemies.

When you see a phantom teleport, prepare to dodge because they will appear in front of you with an empowered, unblockable attack that will leave you vulnerable to a long combo chain. This is even more devastating if you're fighting multiple of them at once.

The phantoms are vulnerable to Aard and Dancing Star bombs, especially during the charge-up for their special attack.

After successfully parrying an attack, you can execute three sword attacks (light or heavy, it doesn't matter) on your target before they recover.

Once you eliminate five of the phantoms, the sixth will attack faster and will only allow one strike after a successful parry.

After defeating the last phantom, a cutscene will trigger, and Geralt will return to the yard of the manor. It's here where she'll comment on what object you placed on her grave.

Blood and Wine is a much bigger expansion than Hearts of Stone, including a brand-new region, Toussaint. And with that, comes even more bosses.

Almost as soon as you arrive in Toussaint, you'll come across a giant named Golyat smashing through a nearby windmill, in a fight against the lovestruck knight Guillaume. You're then forced into a boss fight against Golyat, with the help of Milton and Palmerin.

The Golyat has powerful attacks, but they take him a bit to charge up the power to do so, leaving you time before and after a swing to attack the monster .

Watch out for his slam attack and a sweep that can hit you if you try to flank, both of which you can avoid by dodging backwards.

Using Quen in this fight can be quite useful as the giant does not have too many consecutive attacks. If he breaks your shield, you'll have enough time to use another one before the next hit.

Important Tip: You can kill Golyat instantly by shooting him in the eye with your crossbow. Given he wears a barrel as a helmet, it's a very small target to hit, especially while he's moving. However, successfully killing him this way will give you the David and Golyat achievement .

Once you kill Golyat, you'll receive 450 XP and the Golyat Trophy for Roach, which gives you +5% bonus experience from killing monsters.

Make sure to loot Golyat's corpse after the cutscene for some additional coin and monster parts.

The bruxa is a very tough battle if you aren't prepared and don't know its weaknesses. It has a scream attack that can fling you backwards like Aard and can't be blocked (even with Quen), and it teleports frequently, making it hard to get a hit in.

Important Tip: If you're struggling against the bruxa, you can instantly kill her by placing Yrden on the ground to slow her, and then blasting her with Aard. This will knock her to the ground, letting you quickly run up to the bruxa and deliver a mortal stab.

Firstly, it is weak to Moon Dust bombs, Vampire Oil, and Black Blood potions , so you should prepare these before entering the arena. While these are generally random drops while looting, you should check the Herbalist's Hut near Oxenfurt and Kiera Metz's stock in her hut in Midcopse, both in Velen.

Yrden is great for slowing the bruxa down so you can attack it, while Moon Dust bombs disable its invisibility. You can also place a trap version of Yrden on the ground, which will automatically shoot her when she reappears for some easy bonus damage.

After the vampire is no more, investigate the body on the table to find coins in its mouth and marks that surely can't have been caused by a bruxa alone.

Leave the cellar and Corvo Bianco vineyard to find Palmerin at the tournament grounds to the southwest. Now is a great time to meditate again.

Despite having a health bar that can deplete, don't worry Baron Palmerin de Launfal cannot die during this fight. If his health reaches zero, he'll simply be out of action for the rest of the fight.

Firstly, the shaelmaar is covered in a rocky shell, so hitting it from anywhere other than its front won't do any damage, which is typically only exposed when it's actively attacking you.

However, the shaelmaar is blind and relies on sound to navigate (which is why it was intended to be handicapped by the bells on its tail). Use Aard when standing next to a wall to bait the shaelmaar into rolling into the wall, stunning it and exposing its belly.

Firstly, when attacked, Dettlaff will turn to fog and reappear behind you for a counter attack. When he disappears, you need to dodge forwards (away from where he'll appear).

The beast's second attack is a dash, in which he'll charge at you with his large claws. You should dodge backwards to avoid being hit, and wait until the attack is complete before re-engaging. If you're quick, you can sneak a hit in before Dettlaff starts to block.

Other than avoiding these two attacks, it's wise to maintain a Quen shield and place Yrden down to slow the boss down.

However, as mentioned, you do not need to defeat him to complete the quest. When either of you 'die' in the fight, a cutscene will play where Regis appears and saves you. Regis points out that Geralt’s contract is to stop the beast killing, not necessarily to slay the beast itself, asking you to spare Dettlaff.

You will only have to fight this boss if you choose to, opting against lifting the wight's curse. When you attack the wight, it will flee into the chamber on your right with all the spoons on the floor. Follow her to start a boss fight.

The Spoon Collector is weak to Necrophage Oils, Igni, and Yrden. Igni can stun her, opening her up for attacks, while Yrden slows her down.

The wight is a fairly straightforward boss fight:

It can teleport by hiding in the ground, though there's a delay before it can attack you after re-emerging, which gives you time to dodge it.

It will occasionally shoot poison at you, which you can dodge or negate using Quen.

The fight with the Wicked Witch will start with her summoning an enemy, typically either an Archespore or a Panther. Take the enemy out first, then deal with the witch.

When she starts flying around dropping hot, rancid soup, dodge away or towards the attack to avoid it, and then use Aard when she swoops down to knock her to the ground. Avoid the broom, then attack the witch while she's vulnerable - she doesn't have much health.

You also have to watch out for her pot smash. Once you see her raise her pot, dodge or roll out of the way, otherwise you'll be stunned and the witch will get right back on her broom and send in two more enemies. If you avoided the attack, get into the routine of attacking twice, dodging, then repeating.

At the top you'll face off with the Cloud Giant immediately. His powerful attacks should be avoided at all costs, including a sweeping spin and kick attack. Dodge away to avoid these attacks, and use Quen to absorb any damage you may take.

Periodically, the Cloud Giant will disappear in the cloud beneath you and reappear underneath you, immediately following up with an overhead slam attack. You should dodge to the side to avoid this attack.

Attack the Cloud Giant in the downtime between his attacks.

The alpha garkain is essentially a tougher version of a garkain vampire, and so it's weak to all the same things. Make sure to apply Vampire Oil, craft Black Blood potions, and use Moon Dust and Samum bombs if you can.

This fight with the alpha garkain is similar to fights you've had before with other vampire creatures. His main attack that you'll need to watch out for is a sonic wave that you can see coming, as it needs time to charge it up. Keep your distance or attack before it has the chance to unleash this pulse. Blocking its attacks isn't very effective, so dodging and rolling are your best defensive options.

If you're forced or choose to fight Dettlaff, then prepare for a three-stage boss fight that can be quite the challenge if you don't meet the recommended level of 49. Use the links below to skip to the three boss phases:

Before you begin to fight (while Regis is keeping him busy), prepare by splashing some Vampire Oil on your Silver Sword and equipping your Black Blood potion to use during battle. Also remember that throughout the entire fight, you should constantly be using Quen as it will save you from huge losing chunks of health from some powerful attacks.

Remember fighting Dettlaff back in Blood Run ? This fight is essentially another go at the same fight, at least in the first phase. Here's what you should do:

When Dettlaff turns to smoke and charges at you, dodge to the side to avoid the attack.

Use Aard or Quen's shield break affect to stun Dettlaff.

Dodge Dettlaff's attacks and only attack once you see that he has missed, or he has his back turned.

Continue to dodge and attack up until you get his health bar near the first third. From here, the boss battle will move into the second phase.

Wow, that's uh, quite the transformation. At any rate, getting hit by Dettlaff during this phase can be very deadly. You'll see him cycle through three different attacks. Here's how it works:

First, he will spread his wings in the air, then quickly swoop down and attack. A quick dodge to the side will make this attack nothing to worry about. Alternatively, you can use Aard, Igni, or your crossbow to stun Dettlaff as he dives at you, giving you a brief opportunity to attack him.

Next, Dettlaff will summon a swarm of bats and shoot them in your direction. Roll at the last second to avoid them, otherwise, you'll take a decent chunk of damage and be left stunned.

The final attack is the important one. Detlaff will disappear and burst from under the ground directly beneath you. You'll be able to see it seconds before it hits, so roll and dodge accordingly. Once he is out, he'll be vulnerable for just a few seconds. Give a few slashes, then wait for your next opportunity. This is your main opportunity to attack him during this phase.

There are also pools of blood forming on the ground at random places. Avoid these at all costs! Touching one will get you stuck inside long enough to allow Dettlaff to swoop in and attack with deadly force.

It only makes sense that being transported to another dimension would follow, right? Or are you inside Dettlaff himself? It might be the case, as your goal here is to destroy the three orbs surrounding the area you're in, each one named Dettlaff. Oh, and there's a vampire beast chasing you around too.

The beast chasing you around in the middle is actually quite easy to take down but they deal a lot of damage if they hit you. You'll have to do some dodging and avoiding, but you can take it down relatively quickly. Once defeated, you can head to one of the orbs and start slashing away. The catch is that the vampire will respawn within seconds , only giving you a short window.

The best way to go about this phase is to run to one of the orbs, hit it once or twice, then dodge the vampire's attacks. From there, run to the next orb and repeat the process. The vampire will quickly move to your area, but you should be able to chip away at the orbs this way.

You do not need to defeat the vampire to move onto the next phase.

The fourth and final phase is actually a walk in the park. After returning back to the previous battlefield, run up to Dettlaff and attack to end the battle.

articles.body:
One of the other Draconid species found in The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt is the Wyvern. It can be confused as a dragon, but is much smaller in stature. The Royal Wyvern, a subspecies of the creature, is a bit larger than the standard wyvern, but doesn't have any additional skills.

Most dangerous of all are the royal wyverns. Or, as they're call in some circles, the royal pains in the arse. - Albina Tottelkampf, lecturer in natural scienses at Aretuza

Wyverns are often mistaken for dragons, and, though they are much smaller than their more famous kin and do not breathe fire, they are likewise extremely dangerous monsters. Especially feared are the so-called royal wyverns who, like their namesake monarchs, are exceptionally ornery and extremely deadly.

Wyverns are found in multiple locations, whether guarding treasure, in ruins, or as part of a quest. You'll find a wyvern during Contract: Patrol Gone Missing and Contract: Phantom of the Trade Route . One is being masqueraded as a baby basilisk in The Most Truest of Basilisks . Depending on what route you take you could encounter one in Get Junior .

A wyvern stalks the area to the east of Drahim Castle, just across the lake. Another is found at Guarded Treasure to the northwest of Rannvaig, above and between the two Monster Nest locations on the map.

Like forktails , wyverns are weak to Draconid Oil and Grapeshot bombs. Aard can be used to ground the monster, allowing you to reach it with your coated silver sword. Taking Golden Oriole will prevent the poison damage the lizard can inflict.

Wyverns can drop a red mutagen that increases your Attack power +5% when equipped in the skill tree. This scales up to 20% when linked to corresponding red skills . It's used to craft the Wyvern Decoction in the alchemy tab.

articles.title: Werewolves - The Witcher 3 Guide - IGN

articles.body:
Werewolves are a lore staple when it comes to monsters. It's the same with The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt , though it does have its own unique take on the creature. The title even features a transformation scene during one of the side quests the monster makes an appearance in.

Wolves aren't as bad as they're made out to be. Werewolves, though - they're every bit as bad and worse. - Elsa Vilge, archer

Werewolves are creatures with both men and wolves inside them. When in beastly form, they take the worst traits from each: the wolf's drive to kill and hunger for raw flesh and the man's cruel and calculating intelligence. A werewolf's condition comes about through a curse, and the transformations happen outside his conscious control. When he reverts to human form, he has no memory of his deeds - otherwise he would surely go mad and take his own life.

Werewolves are active at night, particularly when the moon is full. Though they hunt alone, when threatened they will summon wolves to aid them. Werewolves rarely feel the need to flee, for few adversaries put up much of a fight against them. They strike as swiftly as lightning with claws sharp as razors and regenerate any damage received in mere moments. When fighting werewolves a witch should wield a blade covered in oil harmful to the cursed and have a large supply of Devil's Puffballs handy.

A werewolf's curse can at times be lifted, yet there is no universal, surefire method for doing this. A witcher seeking to undertake such a task must therefore equip himself with a great deal of patience - and sturdy armor.

There are a number of ways to encounter a werewolf in the different regions of The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt. Most of these are during the following quests:

You can also run into one of the monsters near the Whispering Hillock in Velen during the Ladies in the Woods main quest.

Fast, superior strength, sharp claws, you'll need to utilize Cursed Oil , Igni , Moon Dust , and Devil's Puffball to defeat a werewolf opponent. High intensity Igni will help cut the healing of your enemy, allowing to stack damage and drain its health easier.

The Werewolf Mutagen grants +5% Attack power when equipped in the skill tree. This scales up to +20% Attack power when linked with all red skills . It's used to craft the Werewolf Decoction .

articles.title: Forktails - The Witcher 3 Guide - IGN

articles.body:
Forktails are the closest thing to dragon you'll encounter in The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt. They are large, scaled, can fly, and have a venomous tail. Though they are often called dragons, forktails cannot breathe fire.

Forktails...Bah! Fuckers'tails're more like cleavers. - Yavinn Buck, veteran of the Mahakaman Volunteer Regiment

Forktails owe their quaint name to the long, sharp growths at the tip of their tails. A blow from this weapon can slice an oaken shield in two - along with the arm that was carrying it. Thus, though its name conjures images of cutlery, fighting a forktail is nothing like a dinner party and ends in death rather than dessert.

There are three quests where you can encounter a forktail.

Forktails are weak to Draconid Oil and Grapeshot bombs. Use Aard to knock them out of the air and keep your space. Golden Oriole to mitigate poison damage inflicted by the stinger on their tail.

Forktails have a blue mutagen that gives +5% Sign intensity when equipped to a skill tree. This buff scales up to 20% depending on the number of blue aligned skills it's linked with. The mutagen's other use is to craft Forktail Decoction in the alchemy tab.

articles.title: Succubi - The Witcher 3 Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Succubi are well known throughout myth for their alluring nature and feeding off sexual energy. The same is true for the creatures found in The Witcher 3: Wild
articles.body:
Succubi are well known throughout myth for their alluring nature and feeding off sexual energy. The same is true for the creatures found in The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt . Succubi are extremely pretty, with the ones in game having lower bodies like a goat. There are two individual succubus you can encounter, one in the wild and the other in the city.

Again?! Good grief, woman, I'm spent... - Lester of Smallton to a succubus, a few days before taking a vow of celibacy

Unlike other monsters, succubi and menads feel no desire to kill, do not crave human blood and usually do not, in fact, mean any harm at all. They are motivated by one thing and one thing only: an insatiable lust. They try in vain to slake this by engaging in sexual acts with any other humanoid species they encounter. While it must be admitted that their "victims" rarely put up much resistance, this does not mean succubi and menads do not present any danger: their never-ending advances, though pleasurable at first, have pushed more than one man to madness or even death.

Succubi and menads usually can be found near human settlements, including small villages and populous cities. They prowl at nigh, though when stricken by serious need they will leave their lairs during the day as well. They shower their affections on men as well as women, the young as well as the old, the ugly as well as the beautiful. Some of them are particularly fond of pastors and other holy men, whose seduction they treat as a sort of game.

Though succubi are peaceful by nature, when forced to fight why will defend themselves fiercely. One should thus not be fooled by their fair appearance - under the velvety skin of their arms lie muscles of iron, and a blow delivered with their rear, goat-like legs or the thick horns on their head can easily crush bone.

There are only two succubus to encounter in The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt.

An unnamed succubus during Practicum in Advanced Alchemy

If you decide to slay a succubus, you'll want to utilize Hybrid Oil and Quen . They are surprisinly hardy, with little weaknesses. The Quen shield will help keep up your health while the oil helps whittle them down faster.

Succubi drop a red mutagen that grants +5% Attack power when equipped. This increases up to +20% when linked with three red skills . Used in alchemy , it is the prime ingredient in the Succubus Decoction .

articles.title: Grave Hags - The Witcher 3 Guide - IGN
articles.summary: While Water Hags are a common enough sight in The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt, their cousin the Grave Hag is a rarer monster. Usually they're found around
articles.body:
While Water Hags are a common enough sight in The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt, their cousin the Grave Hag is a rarer monster. Usually they're found around graveyards, burial sites, or areas that are associated with death. They have an ashen color and are similar in build to water hags.

Cremation, now that's one thing men could learn from gnomes. Burying bodies out in the fields, why, it's like laying out a welcome mat for monsters! Best case scenario, some ghouls will sniff them out, eat their fill and be on their ghoulish way. But if, gods forbid, a grave hag takes to feeding at your cemetery, you'll have no end of trouble. - Jacques de Villepin, Oxenfurt Academy

Few monsters' names fit as well as the grave hags'. As one might guess, these creatures resemble aged, deformed women and loiter near graveyards and battlefields. Grave hags feed on human corpses and in particular on the rotten marrow which they slurp from human bones using their long, prehensile tongues. Once a hag has devoured all corpses within reach, she turns to killing men and burying them in the cemetery as she waits for them to decompose.

There are a few places you can run into a Grave Hag, all tied in with quests.

Unlike most other monsters, grave hags are weak to two signs instead of one. Utilize Yrden and Quen to keep your health up and anchor the hag in place. Follow up with a silver sword coated in Necrophage Oil . Use Black Blood to dish out extra damage if it attaches to you.

Grave Hags drop a green mutagen . It gives +50 Vitality when equipped in the character tab. This scales up to +200 when linked with green skills .

When used in alchemy , it makes the Grave Hag Decoction .

articles.title: Water Hags - The Witcher 3 Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Though they aren't as common as drowners, Water Hags can often be found in similar territories in The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt.  They can be seen near
articles.body:
Though they aren't as common as drowners, Water Hags can often be found in similar territories in The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt . They can be seen near foglets, roaming the fog looking for their next victim. Bilge Hags are a subspecies of water hag and drop the same items as them.

Folk say water hags are drowners' wives. If that be true 'tain't no wonder why they're such ornery bitches. -Shemhel of Dregsdon

Some tales mention water hags and swamp bints masquerading as lost old women to lure travelers back to the rickety shacks they build in the wetlands. In truth, only a blind man, or a sighted man blinded with drink, could mistake the rank sludge and rotting carrion of a water hag's den for a cozy cottage, and the hideous hag herself for an innocent grandmother. Their wrinkled, wart-covered bodies stand nearly two yards tall, with skin the color of a long-dead cadaver and stinking of muck and fish. Bony growths two spans long stick out from their backs, with hair like a tangle of seaweed and claws that would make a werewolf proud completing the picture.

Located primarily in the swamps of Velen, there are a few quests that will bring you in contact with a water hag.

Contract: Muire D'yaeblen on Ard Skellig, Skellige

It may seem a bit backwards, but water hags are weak to Igni , along with the Quen shield negating most of their damage. They have high susceptibility to Northern Wind bombs. As a necrophage, they are vulnerable to Nocrophage Oil

The Water Hag Mutagen is a red variety, bestowing +5% Attack power, up to 20% Attack power when linked with three skills. It is used in alchemy to craft the Water Hag Decoction .

articles.title: Dopplers - The Witcher 3 Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Dopplers are a type of creature that can change its form and appearance in The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt. There are three dopplers you see while playing, two of
articles.body:
Dopplers are a type of creature that can change its form and appearance in The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt . There are three dopplers you see while playing, two of them included in the story. Dudu, a friend of Dandelion and Geralt's appears in the main story. An unnamed doppler is slain when you first enter Novigrad and you only see him during the cut scene. The third is involved in a side quest and the only way to obtain the doppler mutagen.

Your package? Your brother picked it up. You know, you two're damn near identical...Hey! Where you running off to?! - Hanne Kluger, postmaster

Dopplers, also known as vexlings or changelings, are beings able to take on the form of any humanoid or animal they please. This transformation is no mere illusion able to shattered with a simple spell, but an authentic and complete metamorphosis. This means no protective amulets or witcher medallions will signal a doppler's presence - they emanate the same aura as the being whose form they have assumed. This, combined with their incredible intellect and cunning, would make dopplers supreme assassins or thieves - had not nature endowed them with generous and timid spirits which make them avoid the shedding of blood at all costs.

The only enemy doppler is encountered in Contract: An Elusive Thief . At first he's friendly and will remain so if you spare his life. Otherwise, you'll fight him in the streets of Novigard.

Dopplers have a single vulnerability: Relict Oil . It does take a humanoid form so it can be burned with Igni or pushed back with Aard. These aren't considered weaknesses, however.

The red doppler mutagen gives a buff of +5% Attack power. When equipped in the skill tree with red skills this can max out at +20%. Since you can only obtain one mutagen it's either that or use it to craft the Doppler Decoction .

articles.title: Fiends - The Witcher 3 Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Fiends are a large, sturdy Relict that can be found in the forgotten areas of The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt. Appearing like some sort of mutant goat/deer hybrid
articles.body:
Fiends are a large, sturdy Relict that can be found in the forgotten areas of The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt. Appearing like some sort of mutant goat/deer hybrid with three eyes, their visage alone is enough to trigger nightmares.

I regret to inform Your Grace that Your Grace's son fell while hunting a fiend. He died on the spot, along with his squire, his guide, the beaters, his peasant entourage and his hounds. - Kavin Jall, manager of the Villepin Estate near Vizima

Fiends are walking mountains of muscle capped with horned, tooth-filled heads. Like their rarer cousins, bumbakvetches, they live in this forests, swamps and bogs. When possible they avoid humans, but when not possible, they kill them, and without much difficulty.

Their size alone makes fiends and bumbakvetches extremely dangerous - one blow from their powerful paws can kill a horse along with its fully-armored mount. Their enormous heft also makes them invulnerable to Aard: even witchers specializing in the power of Signs could not move one even an inch. Furthermore, any wounds they receive heal at lightning speed.

If that weren't trouble enough, fiends need not rely on their strength and stamina alone when fighting. They can also call on a more refined weapon: the third eye located in the center of their forehead, which they use to draw their pray into a state of hypnosis. During these times their victim does not see anything beyond this single burning eye - the last thing they see before their death.

A fiend's only weakness is its fear of loud noises - bombs such as Samum or Devil's Puffball are this quite effective when fighting this monster. Furthermore, a blade covered in relict oil can increase a witcher's chances of victory - or at least of walking away from the fight.

If you release the evil under Whispering Hillock in Velen during Ladies of the Woods , you'll encounter a fiend during the follow up side quest Return to Crookback Bog . You'll also have to fight a fiend in Skellige during Contract: Missing Son.

Fiends can randomly be encountered east of the hidden treasure to the south of Kimbolt Way.

Weak to Relict Oil , you'll want to coat your silver sword before entering into combat with a fiend. Devil's Puffball and Samum bombs help inflict damage from a distance.

Used to craft the Fiend Decoction , the Fiend Mutagen endows +50 Vitality when equipped in a skill tree . This scales up to +200 Vitality if linked with three green skills.

articles.title: Nightwraiths - The Witcher 3 Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Nightwraiths are the nighttime spectres that branched off from wraiths in The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt. Similar to noonwraiths in appearance, nightwraiths can be
articles.body:
Nightwraiths are the nighttime spectres that branched off from wraiths in The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt . Similar to noonwraiths in appearance, nightwraiths can be seen as female ghosts in a tattered dress. Sometimes the dress will be red and other times it will be gray.

Nightwraiths exude this immense sadness, this helpless wrath... I fear them, same as anyone. But most of all I feel sorry for them. - Aelline Altsparr, elven trobairitz.

Compared to other creatures of the night - katakans, nekurats and werewolves, for example - nightwraiths (and their rarer cousins, duskwraiths) might not seem all that dangerous. After all, one might ask, how much harm could a pale, withered woman in a tattered dress do? The answer: quite a bit. Instead of finding this out the hard way, avoid crossing fields and meadows at night at all costs.

Like noonwraiths, nightwraiths are only found in rural areas. Travelers fall victim to them most often, but if legends are to be believed they also sneak into huts at times and murder peasants in their sleep.

When they attack nightwraiths remain immaterial for most of the time, meaning physical blows pass right through them. They only take on more tangible form for the brief moments in which they strike. When weakened, they will create several projections of themselves which cannot attack directly but act as transmitters of sorts through which the nightwraith can sap her victim's vital energy.

Nightwraiths can turn immaterial and are at such time very difficult to wound. In order to force one to take on corporeal form, trap it with the Yrden Sign or hit it with the blast of a Moon Dust bomb.

Do not believe the old wife tales and think yourself completely safe from nightwraiths during the day. They appear under the light of the sun as well - but are much weaker then than after dusk.

Contract: Jenny o' the Woods is the side quest that will have you encounter a nightwraith.

Like its sun loving cousin, nightwraiths are weak to Yrden , which holds it in place and keeps it solid. It's also vulnerable to Specter Oil and Moon Dust bombs.

The mutagen dropped by Nightwraiths is green in nature, endowing +50 Vitality, up to +200, when equipped and linked with green skills . Outside of this, it's primarily used to make the Nightwraith Decoction in alchemy.

articles.title: Noonwraiths - The Witcher 3 Guide - IGN
articles.summary: A type of specter in The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt, Noonwraiths are female in appearance and materialize while the sun is high. They are often formed from the
articles.body:
A type of specter in The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt , Noonwraiths are female in appearance and materialize while the sun is high. They are often formed from the deaths of women who met horrible ends before their wedding. They're attached to an item that keeps them tied to the mortal plane, usually a memento of their love.

"Despite what is commonly thought, peasants do not interrupt their labors at midday to get out of the run - they do so to avoid noonwraiths." - Vlad Raymond, Peasants and Their Customs

On particularly searing summer days, when the sun reaches its zenith, wraiths will at times appear, resembling sun-scorched women dressed in long, white robes. These are noonwraiths - the spirits of young women and girls who died violent deaths right before their weddings. Driven mad with pain or anger, they wander the fields searching for their unfaithful lovers or backstabbing rivals, though they will kill anyone who does not get our of their way in time. They are often held in this world by some object of intense emotional significance. That is why, if one ever finds a wedding ring or torn veil in the middle of a field, one should not pick it up, but instead back away as quickly as possible.

There are multiple noonwraiths you can encounter, with two of them appearing during Witcher Contracts. The first is during the Contract: Devil by the Well in the Abandoned Village in White Orchard. The second is found near Drakhim Castle in Novigrad during Contract: The White Lady . Both are guaranteed to drop a Noonwraith Mutagen .

Outside of these side quests, noonwraiths can be found near Frischlow and near the Hidden Treasure north of Byways and Elven Ruins Entrance.

As a member of the Specter class, Specter Oil is extremely effective against noonwraiths. Yrden keeps them in solid, allowing you to more easily deal damage with your silver sword. If you're looking to keep your distance, you can hit it with a Moon Dust bomb.

Noonwraiths have a chance to drop a green mutagen that gives +50 Vitality when equipped in a skill tree. The Vitality bonus scales by an additional 50, up to +200, with each green skill the mutagen is linked with.

When not used in a character build, the mutagen is an alchemy ingredient in Noonwraith Decoction .

articles.title: Ekimmaras - The Witcher 3 Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Ekimmaras are a type of vampire you're able to encounter during a couple side quests in The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt. Appearing more monster-like than
articles.body:
Ekimmaras are a type of vampire you're able to encounter during a couple side quests in The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt. Appearing more monster-like than typically portrayed, these are the more common type of vampire you can happen upon.

Bah, ain't nothing to fear. Ekkimaras, why, they ain't nothing more than overgrown bats. - Anonymous city guardsman's last words

Like other vampires, ekimmaras are not, despite what village gossips might say, undead humans. They are instead post-Conjunction monsters who have no particular feelings about garlic, holy water or religious symbols.

Unlike their portrayals in ballads and legends, they look nothing like handsome, pale aristocrats with charming eastern accents, though, like katakans or nekurats, they do bear strong resemblance to overgrown bats. They also do not suck blood from the necks of virgins with a delicate, kiss-like-bite - they tear them to shreds using long, sharp claws and then slurp the splattered blood off the ground.

Ekimmaras are unusually cruel and exceptionally swift. They are able to quickly land blow after blow capable of smashing even the best Mahakaman-made armor into tiny shards. They should be fought with a silver sword, remembering that they regenerate back health over time. One should thus never attempt to tire them out or, gods forbid, wait for them to bleed to death. Instead, cut them down as quickly as possible and, if possible, burn the body to ash and scatter it to the four winds.

There are two side quests where you'll encounter an ekimmara.

Following the Thread - Contract: Monster in the Bits

Like all vampires, Ekimmara are weak to Igni. Using Vampire Oil and Devil's Puffball bombs are also highly effective.

The Ekimmara Mutagen is used in alchemy to brew an Ekimmara Decoction . It increases Vitality by +50 when equipped in a skill tree. When linked with green skills this can max out at +200.

articles.title: Wraiths - The Witcher 3 Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Wraiths are the most common type of specter you'll come across in The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt. Found at cemeteries, crypts, and old ruins, these ghosts can
articles.body:
Wraiths are the most common type of specter you'll come across in The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt . Found at cemeteries, crypts, and old ruins, these ghosts can appear through walls, phase to different areas, and remain immaterial. They drop a mutagen and valuable Specter Dust, used in crafting and alchemy.

Finish all your business before you die. Bid your loved ones farewell. Write your will. Apologize to those you've wronged. Otherwise, you'll never truly leave this world. - Paule Vikar, peasant healer, advice to a dying man

Clerics and scholars are forever debating whether spirits do in fact journey to another world after death, one where eternal joy or suffering awaits. Both groups agree, however, on what happens to spirits who, for one reason or another, remain in our world after their body breathes its last: they transform into wraiths. To hear their mournful howls, one can surmise this is not a fate to be envied.

Wraiths can be commonly found in graveyards, city sewers, and ruins. The very first wraith you can come across is at the White Orchard cemetery to north of the mill. You may get attacked by one outside, but there's a guaranteed wraith that will appear in the mausoleum where you find the witcher corpse for the viper school gear.

Additionally, you can encounter wraiths during the following quests:

Wraiths can also be found north of Blandare at the Guarded Treasure, at the Guarded Treasure to the southwest of Kaer Trolde Harbor and at the guarded treasure near Lofton, Skellige.

Like all specters, wraiths are weak to Specter Oil , Moon Dust bombs, and getting trapped with the Yrden Sign . Additionally, using Quen will maintain your health while you take advantage of the moment they attack, becoming solid enough to hit with your sword without using bombs or Yrden.

The Wraith Mutagen is green and gives +50 Vitality when equipped. That scales an additional +50 Vitality for each green skill it's linked with. When used for alchemy , it's an ingredient for Wraith Decoction .

articles.title: Katakans - The Witcher 3 Guide - IGN
articles.summary: The batlike Katakan are one of the vampiric species of The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt. Rare to stumble upon and hard to kill, these creatures are old and cunning.
articles.body:
The batlike Katakan are one of the vampiric species of The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt . Rare to stumble upon and hard to kill, these creatures are old and cunning. Similar to ekimmaras, the main difference is these monsters can turn invisible, sneak attacking you before you can draw your sword.

Melitele, Great Mother, protect us from evil, from unclean devils and foul demons, and most of all from the clutches of katakans and nekurats... - fragment of a prayer

Katakans and their more dangerous kin, nekurats, are the embodiements of human fear. They hide in the shadows. They feed on blood. They resemble enormous bats - though with long fangs and even longer talons. And, as if that weren't terror enough, they can turn invisible, waiting unseen while dread of their unpreventable attack overwhelms their victim.

There are two locations where you can battle a katakan, both found in the Novigrad region. You'll have to progress through Triss' quests to unlock Now or Never , during which you'll encounter a katakan. The second way to fight the creature is during Contract: The Oxenfurt Drunk .

Like all vampires, katakans are weak to Igni . They are also weak to Yrden , which stops them from going invisible.

They are vulnerable to attacks from a sword coated in Vampire Oil. Both Devil's Puffball and Moon Dust bombs are highly effective.

Drinking down a Black Blood before starting combat is also a good course of action when fighting a vampiric monster.

Katakans can drop a red mutagen, which amps up Attack power by +5% when used in the your character build. This increases to +20% when linked in the tree with red skills . The only other use for the katakan mutagen is in alchemy when brewing Katakan Decoction .

articles.title: How to Watch One Piece in Order
articles.summary: Just in case you have 300+ hours to dedicate to this.
articles.body:
One Piece follows the adventures of Monkey D. Luffy, a boy with a body that responds like rubber thanks to eating a Devil Fruit , on his quest to become the next Pirate King by finding the ultimate treasure of legendary Pirate, Gold Roger. Based on Eiichiro Oda's best-selling manga series, One Piece is full of epic battles and a highly entertaining and eclectic ensemble of characters known as the Straw Hat Pirates.

With over 1,000 episodes across over 20 seasons (divided into 10 sagas with 52 different story arcs), specials, OVAs and shorts, it can be difficult to decide when and where to put the One Piece movies into your (re)watch list. Whether you’re new to the world of One Piece or settling in for an epic movie rewatch alongside the live-action series , we’ve got you covered.

Take a look at our One Piece timeline guide for what order you should watch the One Piece movies and episodes in.

There are currently 15 feature length One Piece movies you can watch alongside the anime series. The movie stories are not connected to the series, and therefore aren’t canon. But the stories are built around canon characters and offer an opportunity to learn more about the world of the Straw Hat Pirates.

While the original One Piece movies are a little hard to track down online, more recent One Piece movies are available to stream on Crunchyroll and also have Blu-ray releases.

If you want to start the true binge (don't be intimidated by that episode number, it's worth it), the One Piece anime is available to stream on Crunchyroll , Hulu , and Netflix . The live-action One Piece show is streaming exclusively on Netflix .

The One Piece Series In Chronological Order

To avoid confusion or early introduction to canon characters, we recommend watching the One Piece movies alongside the anime series and its corresponding episodes in the expansive franchise.

1. One Piece: The Movie (watch after episode 18)

The Straw Hat Pirates find themselves pitted against the ruthless pirate Eldoraggo after an encounter with a trio of thieves. The Straw Hat Pirates must thwart Eldoraggo on his hunt for the treasure of a legendary captain and secure the hoard of gold for themselves. One Piece: The Movie falls in between the Syrup Village arc and the Baratie arc of the East Blue Saga. It offers a good, if visually nostalgic, world overview by showcasing the early days of the crew as they embark on a treasure hunt.

2. One Piece: Clockwork Island Adventure (watch after episode 53)

The Straw Hat Pirates join forces with the Thief Brothers in order to recover their stolen ship, Going Merry and weapons from bandits. The crew and their allies must go to war against the pirate clan reigning over the Clockwork Island, in order to stop their leader from acquiring a superweapon and forcing their crew mate Nami into marriage. One Piece: Clockwork Island Adventure falls after the second half of the Loguetown arc of the East Blue Saga. While this may be a standalone story it's a fun must-watch adventure about a vacation gone awry.

3. One Piece: Chopper’s Kingdom on the Island of Strange Animals (watch after episode 102)

Stories about a great treasure lure the Luffy and the Straw Hat Pirates to the wilderness of Crown Island where the crew encounters intelligent animals. While separate from the rest of the Straw Hats, the crew’s doctor Tony Tony Chopper triggers a prophecy and ends up crowned the island's lord and protector, the King of Beasts. Despite a few interesting fight scenes, Chopper’s Kingdom is an extremely skippable filler film. But if you’re a completionist, One Piece: Chopper’s Kingdom on the Island of Strange Animals falls after episode 102 of the Arabasta Arc: in the Arabasta Saga.

4. One Piece: Dead End Adventure (watch after episode 138)

The Straw Hat Pirates need cash so they enter an underground race between pirates known as the Dead End Competition. The crew finds themselves pitted against a vice-admiral with his own powers and his formidable bounty hunter sidekick. Dead End Adventure is the first full-length feature and offers a fantastic adventure newbies and diehards can enjoy. This movie can be watched at any point after episode 130 but we think it falls in line best after episode 138 in the Goat Island arc of the Sky Island Saga.

5. One Piece: The Cursed Holy Sword (watch after episode 143)

The Cursed Holy Sword centers on Zoro, the crew’s swordsman. While on the island of Asuka, the Straw Hat Pirates learn about a legendary cursed sword the Shichiseiken. The crew’s quickly swept up in the shenanigans of marines intent on freeing the sword. Zoro’s joined their ranks and the rest of the crew must unravel his reasons and figure out what’s going on. This film is a chaotic mess that doesn’t fully come together and is pretty much a miss unless you’re just dying to know more about Zoro. The Cursed Holy Sword falls in line best after episode 14 of the Ruluka Island arc in the Sky Island Saga.

6. One Piece: Baron Omatsuri and the Secret Island (watch after episode 224)

Baron Omatsuri and the Secret Island, the sixth movie in the franchise, see the Straw Hat Pirates interrupt their journey to Grand Line for a pit stop on a recreation island to relax. Upon arrival the leader of the island, Baron Omatsuri, welcomes them and gives them seven challenges to achieve greater relaxation. The remainder of the movie is unraveling the mystery lurking beneath the surface of this seemingly happy community. Without giving anything away for the uninitiated, it's safe to say the Secret Island should not be on your skip list. The Secret Island falls in line best after episode 224 of the Ocean’s Dream arc in the Water 7 Saga.

7. One Piece: The Giant Mechanical Soldier of Karakuri Castle (watch after episode 228)

If you’re in the mood for great action sequences and an off-kilter plotline, then The Giant Mechanical Soldier of Karakuri Castle will fully satisfy. The Straw Hats find and open a treasure box. Instead of loot, the crew finds an old lady inside. They agree to help her return home in exchange for a treasure on her Mecha Island. Upon arrival, the crew comes under attack by the island’s leader before he reverses track and asks for their help finding the treasure. Karakuri Castle is best seen after episode 228 of the Foxy’s Return arc in the Water 7 Saga.

8. One Piece – Episode of Arabasta: The Desert Princess and the Pirates (watch after episode 312)

Most One Piece fans will list the Arabasta arc as one of the best in the franchise. Which means if you watched the episodes, then this movie is extremely skippable. This movie is essentially a condensed version of that storyline that doesn’t offer any new storywise. If you need or want a refresher offered with high quality action sequences then watch the Episode of Arabasta remake after episode 312.

9. One Piece: Episode of Chopper Plus: Bloom in Winter, Miracle Sakura (watch after episode 325)

The Chopper Plus remake changes events and adds new canon characters, including a sidekick for the villain Wapol, to the original episodes in the Drum Island arc. It’s best to view watch this One Piece movie as an alternate universe where Luffy’s still trying to save crewmate Nami with different obstacles. If you’re interested in seeing the Bloom in Winter play out in a parallel world, watch Chopper Plus after episode 325 and the end of the Water 7 Saga.

10. One Piece Film: Strong World (watch after episode 381)

Luffy and his crewmates learn that islands in East Blue have been destroyed. The crew discovers that an ex-member of the Rocks Pirates, Shiki the Golden Lion, is responsible. Shiki wants to destroy the marines. After he kidnaps Nami to become their navigator, the Straw Hats decide to take matters into their own hands. They come together to battle the legendary Shiki and rescue Nami. Strong World showcases Shiki’s devil fruit powers and pits Luffy and crew against a myriad of challenges. Strong World is absolutely not canon but makes for a great ride. Watch it any time after episode 381. But we suggest waiting until after the last episode (429) of Little East Blue arc of the Summit Saga for best alignment in this epic journey.

11. One Piece 3D: Straw Hat Chase (watch after episode 381)

One Piece 3D: Straw Hat Chase gets treated as the eleventh movie in the One Piece franchise, but in reality it’s more of a short (and at this point, kind of lost media). Luffy wakes up to a missing crew and spends the entire movie on the hunt for them. Cue it up directly after finishing Strong World because there’s nothing special to separate it from the pack. Straw Hat Chase is pretty much impossible to find and so skippable not even hardcore completionists will demand you sit through it.

12. One Piece Film: Z (watch after episode 578)

One Piece Film: Z aims right for the feels with a story centering former marine admiral Z. Z’s stolen a dangerous weapon known as the “Dyna Stones,” and now the Straw Hat Pirates and other admirals must battle him to stop the end of the world. Widely considered one of the best One Pieces movies, Z is colorful and action-packed on top of being a tear-jerker. There’s a bit of debate about the best time to slide Z into the timeline. It’s viewers choice: cue it up after episode 573 or wait until the end of the Z’s Ambition arc with episode 578. Whichever you decide, not watching it would be a mistake.

13. One Piece Film: Gold (watch after episode 750)

The Straw Hat Pirates visit the greatest entertainment city contained on the Gran Tesoro ship. THe story shifts from a gambling vacation to a heist film in short order. This casino adventure offers slick animation and plenty of action from start to finish. Sometimes the point is fan service and that’s exactly the aim of Gold. If you’re this far down the One Piece rabbit hole then that fan service is going to make for a satisfying ride. This is best viewed after finishing the Silver Mine arc of the Whole Cake Island Saga.

14. One Piece: Stampede (watch after episode 889)

Luffy and crew decide to participate in a pirate festival alongside numerous other famous pirates. They quickly realize it's actually a free-for-all to find another one of Roger’s treasures. Over the course of the battle royale, more mysterious goings-on appear and cause upheaval. Do expect to see plenty of fan favorite characters, and the full range of powers operation in the One Piece World. Stampede is next-level fan service wrapped in an epic adventure. This must see movie can be watched any time after episode 889, the end of the Whole Cake Saga. But we suggest maybe waiting until after the Cidre Guild arc in the Wano Country Saga.

15. One Piece Film: Red (watch after episode 1030)

One Piece Film: Red, the most recent movie, is about Shanks and his daughter Uta. The Straw Hats attend a concert hosted by Uta, a famous singer, on Elegia the Island of Music. Things quickly go awry when the attendees discover that Uta is the daughter for Shanks, chief of the Red Hair Pirates. It should be noted that Red is initially driven by songs since that’s how Uta’s power manifests but the unfolding mysteries, chases, displays of legendary powers, and dangerous encounters make it all worthwhile. Red fits seamlessly after the Uta's Past arc of the Wano Country Saga.

How to Watch One Piece Movies in Release Order

Chopper’s Kingdom on the Island of Strange Animals (2002)

Baron Omatsuri and the Secret Island (2005)

Giant Mecha Soldier of Karakuri Castle (2006)

The Desert Princess and the Pirates: Adventures in Alabasta (2007)

Episode of Chopper Plus: Bloom in the Winter, Miracle Cherry Blossom (2008)

Eiichiro Oda has been teasing that he’s almost done with the One Piece manga for about 15 years, yet here we are. Though no one has a clear idea of when the manga (and therefore the anime) will end, we do know a few years. At a Jump Festa event in December 2025, Oda teased the end of the Elbaph arc for 2026 and said “The story will be moving at a breakneck speed.”

The One Piece anime is going through big changes this year, as it is changing from a weekly to a seasonal release schedule and will only release a maximum of 26 episodes per year starting this April with the Elbaph arc adaptation. We still don’t know when the next One Piece movie is going to come out, but Oda said it is not going particularly well production-wise. Still, he teased at Jump Festa that the story is one “all of you will be very interested in.”

There’s also an upcoming remake of One Piece titled “The One Piece” which is in production, as well as a LEGO One Piece special coming to Netflix.

While we don't have any news about new One Piece movies, we do already have all eight episodes of Season 2 of the live action series available on Netflix. We've also gotten confirmation that Season 3 has already been greenlit .

Another major One Piece collaboration is LEGO releasing seven new One Piece sets based on the first season of the Netflix show. All of these sets represent scenes from the East Blue Saga.

articles.summary: Sony’s Pulse Elevate wireless gaming speakers are launching on November 12th and will cost $219.99, the company announced on Tuesday. Preorders begin on September 1st.
articles.body: Sony’s Pulse Elevate wireless gaming speakers are launching on November 12th and will cost $219.99, the company announced on Tuesday. Announced nearly a year ago, the speakers are compatible with a PS5, PlayStation Portal, PC, and Mac, and they include “studio-inspired planar magnetic drivers” that offer “lifelike sound across the entire audible spectrum,” Sony says. They also include a built-in mic for voice chat, Sony’s PlayStation Link low-latency tech, and charging docks for topping up the batteries. [Media: The Pulse Elevate speakers come in two colors, black and white, and preorders begin on September 1st at 10AM ET in the US or 10AM local time elsewhere. The black speakers will be available to buy globally on the PlayStation Direct website and at “participating retailers.” The white speakers will only be available on PlayStation Direct in the US, UK, France, Germany, Austria, Belgium, Luxembourg, Netherlands, Italy, Spain, and Portugal, and in other regions at “select” retailers.

If you've tried the Axion, there's a good chance you're all too familiar with its rather jarring vertical recoil, which makes staying on target difficult, especially when ADS. To help combat this, I've created a build that minimizes the recoil while also slightly boosting its damage range and bullet velocity at the cost of some ADS speed, which I think is a fair compromise.

Here's our recommended best attachments for the Axion:

As of Season 1, the Cronen Osprey is without a doubt the best Assault Rifle in Modern Warfare 4. With the right attachments it offers very minimal recoil and an incredibly fast TTK that will melt your opponents.

The second best AR, in my opinion, is either the M4 or the highly underrated Hyeon Burst , which, with the right attachments, absolutely beams enemies from any distance. While it's a little on the slower side to get started, once it gets going, your enemies simply won't stand a chance. It received a small nerf shortly after launch, but in our opinion it's still one of our top picks.

Quick Fix for immediately triggering health regeneration when killing players or Ghost if you want to stay undetected by Enemy Callouts, UAVs, Portable Radars, and Heartbeat Sensors.
