articles.body:
A popular Nintendo blogger who tells his viewers obscure facts about Super Mario has been hit with serious health conditions, including heart failure. The online personality has vowed to continue running the blog for as long as he’s able.

Supper Mario Broth is a blog and series of social media accounts known for posting arcane and funny trivia about everyone’s favorite Italian plumber. The blog has shared thousands of facts from the series since its creation in 2012.

In The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for Nintendo Switch 2, it is possible to play the ocarina using Dry Bones in Super Mario Maker 2. — Supper Mario Broth (@MarioBrothBlog) November 5, 2026

In The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for Nintendo Switch 2, it is possible to play the ocarina using Dry Bones in Super Mario Maker 2.

“I am scared I will soon not be able to see Mario again,” he said in a post to his 270,000 X / Twitter followers. “However, I promise that until that day arrives, I will always be here, posting Mario facts. Thank you all so much for your support through the years.”

Despite a healthy lifestyle, the condition is genetic. According to the blogger, there’s a two-in-three chance he survives past one year.

The condition is also affecting his eyesight, degrading it over time. He isn’t sure whether surgery or medication can stop or slow this process yet.

“Since being able to see well is fundamental to my ability to both myself research Mario games and compile the discoveries of others, this may affect my ability to run Supper Mario Broth in the future,” he said. “However, I will never forget the promise I made to you: I will continue to run Supper Mario Broth for as long as I’m physically able to.”

The blogger continued to say that “sharing [Mario] findings is my only purpose,” but noted that the condition may cause gaps in the content.

Supper Mario Broth didn’t ask for any financial or emotional support in this difficult time. “I already have all the support I could need,” he said. “All I can do is hope for my frail body to overcome this.

“I hope with all my (failing) heart that I can continue doing this for years to come,” he said. “And if I should one day stop posting: thank you very much for reading.”

Thousands of supportive replies have poured in, thanking the blogger for his work and integrity. There’s fan art, messages of support, and even people pressuring Nintendo to let the blogger play whatever in-development Mario game it’s cooking up.

Photo by BEHROUZ MEHRI/AFP via Getty Images.

Kirk McKeand is a Contributor on IGN News. Find him on Twitter @MckKirk

articles.title: As GTA 6 Preload Goes Live, Fans Dig Into the Data to Try to Unearth Unannounced Information Ahead of Launch
articles.summary: GTA 6 preloads are live for those who live in New Zealand (or are pretending to live in New Zealand to play early) and fans are scanning the game files for new information.
articles.body:
GTA 6 preloads are live for those who live in New Zealand (or are pretending to live in New Zealand to play early) and fans are scanning the game files for new information. Of course, the files are encrypted so they can only tell us so much.

The main takeaway is how much space each of the things in GTA 6 takes up. Rockstar has announced that GTA 6 weighs in at up to 212 GB, “depending on your device.” But following the release of the preload today, it was reported that the audio file alone is 22GB.

Elsewhere, one Rockstar fan believes that because the files for story content are separated out from the main game files, the same will be true for the inevitable next version of GTA Online. This would suggest that you’ll eventually be able to install single-player and Online separately.

An account focused on reporting PlayStation game file sizes also noticed “intentType": "launchMultiplayerActivity," seemingly confirming Online’s eventual appearance in GTA 6. Rockstar has been completely silent on the existence of GTA Online for GTA 6, but the enduring success of GTA 5’s online portion means it’s safe to assume it’ll happen at some point.

Interestingly, a file named "core_restofworld001" is missing from the Australia & New Zealand version of GTA 6, perhaps suggesting there's cut content in those regions. Another fan noticed that BVH8 will be supported in GTA 6. BVH8 specifically makes ray tracing work better on PS5 Pro, which Ubisoft used for Assassin’s Creed Shadow’s PS5 Pro support.

“By itself, the PS5 Pro's faster GPU helps performance without much effort from developers, but the game changing technology is the improved ray tracing capabilities of the PS5 Pro that BVH82 offers over BVH4,” Ubisoft said at the time. “With our implementation of BVH8 support on PS5 Pro, we were able to speed up GPU tasks involving hardware ray tracing usage by about 300%.”

Officially, all we know about PS5 Pro support is the confirmation from Sony that GTA 6 will feature “PS5 Pro Enhanced Support.” Unfortunately, there’s been no word on what exactly that means. Indeed, Rockstar has yet to announce resolution and frame rate details for GTA 6 on any platform.

However, those hoping for higher frame rates might be disappointed. According to experts, it’s unlikely GTA 6 will go higher than 30fps on any platform because of its ray tracing and physics simulations.

While you wait for GTA 6’s November 19 launch, there’s still a small chance you might be able to bag some GTA 6 merch from Selfridges , but it’s selling out fast. And we've got all the information you need on the GTA 6 preload global release times , as well as details on the physical poster.

Kirk McKeand is a Contributor on IGN News. Find him on Twitter @MckKirk

articles.title: Christopher Nolan’s Interstellar Is Getting a LEGO Set
articles.summary: LEGO has approved a LEGO Ideas submission based on the Christopher Nolan movie Interstellar. It will become an official LEGO set at some point in the future.
articles.body:
LEGO has announced the winners of the LEGO Ideas First 2026 Review Stage. These sets originated as fan designs through the LEGO Ideas program, and have now been approved for official release. Among the newly announced upcoming sets is one based on the Christopher Nolan movie Interstellar. The other two sets to get approval during this review stage were Tulip Field Windmill and Chinese Cork Carving Art. As yet, there’s no word on pricing or official release dates for the newly approved sets.

LEGO Ideas Sets Approved for Official Release

Tulip Field Windmill by HisBrickMaterials

The Interstellar set was submitted by fan designer Minibrick41587 . It includes the wedge-shaped Ranger spacecraft from the movie, along with minifigures for the Matthew McConaughey character Cooper and the Anne Hathaway character Dr. Brand. Also included are the robot companions TARS and CASE.

While Interstellar wasn't immediately appreciated as one of Christopher Nolan's best films after its 2014 release (we gave it an 8/10 in our review ), there's been a growing appreciation for the film in recent years among fans and critics. This LEGO set's approval may be another sign of its improving standing.

New Additions to the LEGO Ideas Parking Lot

During this latest review stage, LEGO placed two additional LEGO Ideas submissions in the Parking Lot. These sets are The 5th Element, which features a flying taxi and a Multi Pass from the movie, and Peashooter, based on a weapon from the video game Plants vs. Zombies. The Parking Lot is where sets go when they “need a little longer to work through the review process.” They’ll stay in the Parking Lot until a final decision is made.

Parking Lot sets may end up being approved or not. But a set being put in the Parking Lot doesn’t say anything about its quality. The recently approved LEGO Daft Punk set had previously been in the Parking Lot.

We’ve just about reached the end of the line for new 2026 LEGO releases. The only remaining set scheduled to come out this year is the 2026 Black Friday LEGO set, LEGO Godzilla . However, a number of sets have been announced for January 2027 and beyond; see our running list of every upcoming LEGO set announced so far for more info.

Chris Reed is a senior commerce editor and deals expert for IGN. He also runs IGN's LEGO coverage and maintains the upcoming release dates articles for video games , LEGO sets , and 4K Blu-rays . You can follow him on Bluesky .

articles.title: ‘Even if Someone Does Get It Running on PC, That’s Not Going to Be a Good Experience’ – Why AI Cloning Won’t Sink GTA 6’s Launch, but Could Reshape Game Development
articles.summary: Will AI-made PC ports impact GTA 6's launch? The experts say no, but vibe-coding is here to reshape the games industry as we know it.
articles.body:
Something new is happening in the world of video games. On that much at least, we can mostly agree.

A new generation of agentic AI coding tools has unleashed a tsunami of mash-ups and ports and reverse-engineered remakes that have been generating nonstop headlines over the past six weeks. You know the ones: Halo playable in a browser . Minecraft playable inside Twitter . Insomniac's Spider-Man web-slinging through Rocksteady's Arkham City .

What we seem much less able to agree on is what this all means, whether it's good or bad, and what might come next. For some, this is a huge technological breakthrough, while for others it's the dawn of a slop era for gaming.

This uncertainty is made more tense by the fact that these stories poke at some of the most raw and sensitive spots in gaming discourse: AI ethics, game preservation, the games industry labour market and its endless cycles of layoffs, and the end of disc-based game ownership. Depending on which lens you're looking through, you might see a story about an AI port as part of a much larger narrative about environmentally ruinous datacenters, a new era of game preservation, or a welcome middle finger to a platform holder that wants to sell you a code in a box.

The result is that everyone's wound up, but for very different reasons. So, to try to figure out what's going on, where it might go from here, and whether the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6 is about to be torpedoed by it all, I spent hours talking with a host of smart and well-placed people representing a range of perspectives on this story.

"How many cease and desist letters do we need to send out?"

As the head of Nightdive Studios, Stephen Kick knows a thing or two about ports and reverse engineering. Since 2012, he and his colleagues have produced dozens of high-profile remasters, including System Shock 2, Star Wars: Dark Forces, and the upcoming Thief: The Dark Project Remastered. "Yeah, AI has definitely been the topic of conversation," Kick explains.

For Nightdive, there's clear utility in a tool that can take the opaque, machine-readable code of an existing game and reverse engineer it into something you can edit and enhance and tinker with. This is exactly what models like Anthropic's Opus 5.5 seem to be really quite good at, and it's how vibe coders have been creating eye-catching clips of Mario clobbering Margit The Fell Omen . While Kick stresses that "for the past year or so we've not been using it," he does see the technology as a promising accelerant for the kind of work his teams do.

Kick suspects that those vibe-coded remakes, ports, and mash-ups, however, will be generating some serious anxiety for bigger players in the industry right now. "I can't even imagine what the lawyers are going through right now with all the major publishers." He imagines a flurry of panic: "What do we do? How many cease and desist letters do we need to send out? How can we capitalize on this? How can we integrate this into our own business model right now?"

And he suspects that the scope of the impending clampdown may be much more far-reaching than a few takedown notices – it could represent yet another attempt to redefine what game ownership looks like. "One of the things that I foresee is that game developers will no longer be actually giving you a copy of the game," Kick says. "You'll have to stream the game now because they don't want any of those files out at all because anybody anywhere can take them and reverse engineer them in a matter of hours."

"The bottom line for Grand Theft Auto 6"

So what does all this mean for the biggest game of the year, Grand Theft Auto 6? A succession of breathless commentators have predicted GTA 6 will be one of the biggest entertainment launches of all time , so it's fair to say that Rockstar and parent company Take-Two Interactive have a lot at stake. You might imagine they'd be pretty concerned about launching a console exclusive during a period where that exclusivity now means nothing to those with access to AI. That’s certainly on the mind of Obbe Vermeij, former Rockstar North technical director.

“I think I would be concerned, if I was Rockstar, that somebody would just take the PS5 version and get AI to change it to PC, which won't be won't be as good as their effort, but it could still also hurt their sales,” he told Rock Paper Shotgun in a recent interview.

Vermeij’s concerns aren’t based on nothing. “People are playing Demon’s Souls on PC and it’s a PlayStation 5 exclusive,” explained Digital Foundry’s Richard Leadbetter during an interview with The Games Business . “It’s choppy, it looks horrible, but Marvel’s Wolverine is running on a PC. So there’s all of that to contend with.”

“But let’s be clear here: the genie’s out of the bottle,” he said. “And Anthropic isn’t the only player in the game. They might have issues with all of this stuff, but let’s say the Chinese models are eight months away from doing the same thing. What’s going to stop them? OpenAI, what’s going on there? I’d say it’s problematic.”

All that considered, I chatted with James McWhirter and Liam Deane, a pair of senior analysts in the games division at market research and intelligence firm Omdia. They've both been tracking the development of these technologies, so I asked them directly: Will vibe coders ultimately bring GTA 6 to PC before the official port?

According to the analysts: nah, probably not. "The bottom line for Grand Theft Auto 6 is that it's too early for this technology to seriously disrupt the game's launch," says Deane. "Even if someone does get the PS5 version running on PC, in the short term that's not going to be a good experience. It's going to be an interesting tech demo for some people if it does happen, but I think realistically it's not going to be a way of playing a game that will be attractive to 99% of players."

"If GTA 6 was launching a year from now, the picture might be quite different. But it's just about getting out in time."

If all that's true, you might wonder why reports currently point to GTA 6 launching for PC as early as the first quarter of 2027. That would be a pretty speedy turnaround, given that GTA 5 took more than 18 months to launch on PC. Has Take-Two moved that date forward, as some have speculated, in a bid to beat AI ports to the punch?

Again, the analysts are dubious. "It was probably a reaction to the memory crisis more than anything," explains McWhirter. "GTA 6 was meant to be the game that would help drive sales of PS5 and Xbox Series X and S, but instead those consoles have become supply constrained because of shortages of key components – namely memory and storage. That means that Rockstar needs to look at ways of expanding their audience, which means the PC release suddenly becomes a lot more important in terms of broadening the addressable market for the game."

In other words, Rockstar already has a whole host of reasons to bring GTA 6 to PC pretty darn fast. If that does come to pass (and it's worth remembering that a PC release hasn't even been announced yet) it isn't necessarily a symptom of AI heebie-jeebies.

So everything is actually fine and dandy and everybody is getting worked up over nothing? Not quite. Because while agentic AI might not be able to get GTA 6 running on PC right now, it can certainly clone an indie game in record time, and even beat a small studio to market based on their own prerelease demo. This issue has turned Steam Next Fest – which usually features thousands of playable demos from unreleased games – into a huge risk for independent developers.

To find out more about how AI is affecting small studios, I reached out to Rami Ismail. As well as working as a consultant and speaker, he's perhaps best known as the co-founder of Vlambeer, the two-person studio that was responsible for Nuclear Throne, Ridiculous Fishing, and Luftrausers. I wondered whether the threat of cloning might be affecting how indies think about showcasing their games. His answer is a firm yes.

"Developers are arguing about whether we can still do the thing that players want us to do, which is to post about our games early," Ismail tells me. "Because there are now companies that have AI agents that are scouring social media. These people aren't even doing it themselves – their AI agents are scouring social media, searching for games that are gaining momentum. If they find one, the AI will ask itself whether it can clone it well, and if the answer is yes it will clone the game."

"What are we supposed to do on our end? What can an indie developer do?"

You might argue that indie developers could make use of generative AI themselves to develop their own games more quickly and with less financial risk. It's certainly true that it's hard for tiny studios to turn down tools that might give them any kind of advantage. And as the use of gen-AI becomes more widespread, it will take more and more conviction to remain committed to AI-free workflows in an ultra-competitive (and increasingly clone-filled) market. But on the other hand, Ismail tells me, indies that make use of generative AI will be profoundly vulnerable to changes in the cost and availability of those tools.

He asks me to imagine an indie dev who uses an AI coding tool to build a feature for their game. The resulting code is hard to parse and extremely long, but it works. "That isn't much of a problem because right now tokens are subsidized, and people can pay something like $99 for a Claude or OpenAI subscription," Ismail explains. "But now, imagine there's a bug, and you need to fix it. And imagine the AI company goes, okay, now the $99 subscription is no longer there. That's now a $1,400 subscription, and you pay X amount of money per token." Big studios with corporate backing might be able to soak up the cost or negotiate bespoke pricing, but indies would be in a much more precarious position.

And if your game's codebase is sprawling and no longer especially human-readable, you're left with little choice but to suck it up and pay the extra money. Or fold.

If you've read Cory Doctorow's writing on the subject – or just used the internet at any point in the last decade – you might recognise the scenario Ismail's describing as a textbook example of 'enshittification' , the process by which a service goes from prioritising the needs of its users to ever more aggressively prioritising shareholder value at the expense of all else. "So this is all an incredible replication of the rideshare model, where you just undercut the taxis until the taxis are gone, and then you enshittify your product," Ismail says. "But it's being speedrun at a scale I've never seen before."

As for what comes next, there's uncertainty and disagreement here, too.

At the start of this piece, I explained that Stephen Kick foresaw a future where cloud streaming is the only way to access your games. When I put this idea to Omdia, I find they're sceptical. "Cloud may not necessarily be the end-goal for publishers as it remains unproven as a delivery vehicle for premium triple-A console and PC games," says McWhirter. "But platform holders and publishers will take game security more seriously. For instance, it's highly likely PlayStation is using cutting-edge frontier AI models to identify vulnerabilities in its console's firmware and patch them before the modding community can exploit them."

If one thing feels like a safe bet, it's that these tools are only going to get more powerful. They've developed at a seemingly exponential rate in a short span of time, after all. Of the people I spoke to, Rami Ismail is the odd one out in expressing scepticism here. He believes there might actually be much less headroom for improvement than you might think. "We could arguably still make AI more efficient. That is the thing we can do, but we've already fed pretty much the entire corpus of human civilization into these devices, right? There's nothing left."

"The only thing that I'm seeing right now that could meaningfully increase the corpus of these datasets is if these AI companies start hiring – directly or indirectly via proxies or middlemen – the people that they're displacing from the labor market to make stuff directly for AI," Ismail tells me. "And we're actually seeing this among indie developers. There's a massive wave of emails that we're all getting that say, 'hey, do you want to sell your codebase?'"

So, if there's one thing we can say with certainty about the intersection of AI and gaming, it's that the future is probably going to be messy and weird. At the time of writing, Anthropic has just taken its first steps to restrict Claude's ability to clone video games . Whether that dam will hold very much remains to be seen. My sense is that this change won't do much to change the opinion of any of the interviewees I spoke with, whether they're excited or depressed by the idea of an AI future.

"As a creator, I think for me it's very clear," Ismail tells me. "I really like my work. And so I like doing my work. I just like programming, and if that makes me slower, then I will be like the artisan table maker that sells slightly more expensive tables than everybody else, right?" In the months and years ahead, we'll see what exactly kinds of projects, pricing models, and platform holder countermeasures players are willing to support or tolerate. And which they won't.

James Nouch is a freelance writer who has written for Rock Paper Shotgun and GamesRadar+ among many other video game websites and magazines.

articles.title: Sony’s new PlayStation Portal handheld includes ‘additional’ internal storage
articles.summary: The Japan-only model arrives on December 10th in a midnight black color scheme.
articles.body: Sony is launching a new version of its PlayStation Portal exclusively in Japan next month. The updated model will launch in the midnight black color option we’ve seen before, and will include “additional” internal storage for future-looking features. It’s the additional internal storage that’s the surprise change to this particular model, which will be locked to Japanese language options and can only be used with a PlayStation account registered in Japan. Sony says the extra storage is for “future functionality” that it will announce once these features are finalized. [Media: Sony is also renaming this particular Portal from PlayStation Portal Remote Player to PlayStation Portal Player. The name change, combined with extra internal storage, seems to suggest that this particular model might get access to streaming apps. The existing PlayStation Portal doesn’t support streaming apps like YouTube, Disney Plus, or Netflix, and is primarily designed to stream PS5 games from a console or the cloud. The PlayStation Portal isn’t powerful enough to play PlayStation games locally, but extra storage could also let you sync media for offline playback. This Japan-only PlayStation Portal is launching on December 10th, priced at 39,980 yen (around $253).

articles.title: LEGO Teases Yoshi Set for 2027
articles.summary: Nintendo has teased a new LEGO Yoshi set in a post on the Nintendo Today! app.
articles.body:
Nintendo has teased a new LEGO Yoshi set.

A news update posted to the Nintendo Today! app on Monday, November 9 is labelled "New LEGO Super Mario Set Hatching Soon," with the subtitle "Adults Welcome." Clicking into the post reveals a full chunk of Yoshi’s face in plastic brick form.

The teaser confirms that the set is a new addition to the Super Mario theme, owing to the rideable dinosaur’s debut in Super Mario World. However, the 'adult' focus of the teaser suggests the Super Mario line is branching out into more complex sets built for display.

There’s no word on pricing or release date, but based on the copyright information, we expect LEGO Yoshi to release in early 2027.

The LEGO Super Mario theme currently has about 20 sets in rotation , but well over 100 sets have been released since the lined first debuted in 2020. The previously released LEGO Mario & Yoshi set , which evokes a retro pixel art look, is set to join the most of those sets in retirement this December. Apparently LEGO can only handle own Yoshi at a time.

The Super Mario theme has generally stuck to the old-school ethos of being built for interactive play, the bulk made up of smaller sets with one or two minifigures. In recent years, however, the company has branched out with larger decorative builds for adult fans.

I think it’s safe to say we’re looking at a giant LEGO Yoshi, which falls into the latter category. The closest approximation that currently exists in the Super Mario line is the Mario Kart sets dedicated to Mario and Luigi, priced at $179.99 and $169.99, respectively.

The Super Mario Galaxy Movie: Yoshi Egg Playset Image Gallery

While LEGO generally sticks to modern depictions of the Super Mario characters, the company has also experimented with sets like the LEGO Donkey Kong Arcade . The 'hatching' reference may just be for marketing’s sake, but it would be cool to see LEGO try and replicate something like the Hatchin Yoshi toy that was released alongside The Super Mario Galaxy Movie .

Like Nintendo, LEGO is generally trying to balance its appeal across generations with different 'levels' of sets. The LEGO Pokemon theme , for example, originally launched with three massive and particularly expensive builds dedicated to individual pocket monsters. A year later, the toy company released more than a dozen smaller (and cheaper) Pokemon sets using its new Smart Play technology . The strategy generally feels like "here’s one for the adults," then "here’s some for the kids."

The challenge with the more adult-focused sets is they’re significantly more expensive. LEGO uses a relatively standard "price ber brick" model for its sets, which have only gotten bigger with time . Still, the strategy seems to be working well for LEGO, who reported record-breaking revenue in the first half of 2026.

Blythe (she/her) is an Audience Development Coordinator at IGN who spends way too much time in character customization screens and tracking down collectibles.

articles.title: Get Ready for the First New Scott Pilgrim Comic in 16 Years
articles.summary: The first new Scott Pilgrim comic in 16 years is almost upon us. Feast your eyes on this exclusive preview of Scott Pilgrim EX: Dawn of Metal Scott #1.
articles.body:
2026 may be rapidly winding down, but we're still looking ahead to one of the most eagerly anticipated new comics of the year. Scott Pilgrim EX: Dawn of Metal Scott #1 is the first new comic in the beloved franchise since 2010's Scott Pilgrim's Finest Hour. And luckily, IGN has a new preview of this monumental release.

Check out the slideshow gallery below to see the first seven pages of Scott Pilgrim EX: Dawn of Metal Scott #1:

Scott Pilgrim EX: Dawn of Metal Scott #1 Preview Gallery

Scott Pilgrim EX: Dawn of Metal Scott #1 is written and drawn by series creator Bryan Lee O'Malley. The comic serves as a prequel to the recent arcade-style brawling game Scott Pilgrim EX (which also technically makes it a sequel to the 2023 Netflix series Scott Pilgrim Takes Off). Here's the official description for this issue:

Scott met Ramona. Sparks flew. The two of them had to work together in order to defeat Ramona's Seven Evil Exes and their nefarious leader, Gideon Gordon Graves. Some other stuff happened in various media formats that may or may not be canon. That's all in the past. These days, Scott and Ramona are a happy couple, and the Exes have moved on from their unhealthy obsessions. I guess they all got therapy or whatever. Now, after a period of peace, a new threat is about to emerge. Are our heroes ready? Let's find out!!!

“When I was asked to create a minicomic for SCOTT PILGRIM EX, I quickly said yes without considering the implications,” said O’Malley in a statement. “Only when I started writing and drawing it did I realize this would be the first new Scott Pilgrim comic in 16 years. It’s only a trifle, but returning to Scott’s Toronto really did feel like coming home.”

Scott Pilgrim EX: Dawn of Metal Scott #1 will be released on November 11. You can preorder a copy at your local comic shop .

In IGN's Scott Pilgrim EX review , Will Borger writes, "Scott Pilgrim EX is the latest in a long line of retro revivals from Tribute Games, and like all of its previous works, the developer has done an admirable job of producing a beat ‘em up that builds on its predecessor while adding much appreciated gameplay depth and plenty of replayability. I love EX’s RPG systems (simple as they are), its world, and how there is always another interesting character to try when I get bored. But it’s also a game that grapples with the passage of time, even if it perhaps doesn’t mean to. The modern beat ‘em up exists because of the games that came before, but they were often far more limited. With the passage of time, we’ve returned to those ideas and refined them. Like Scott Pilgrim itself, those games have gone from something that was new to something that is now referenced. Nostalgia is a powerful drug, but a bittersweet one, and Scott Pilgrim EX understands that. You can go back in time, but you can’t go back to the way things were. All that’s left is to appreciate where you’ve been and enjoy what’s here now. And you know what? What’s here is pretty fun."

Jesse is a mild-mannered staff writer for IGN. Allow him to lend a machete to your intellectual thicket by following @jschedeen on BlueSky .

articles.title: Former BioWare Executive Producer Mark Darrah Shares Original Vision for a More 'Immersive' Dragon Age 4
articles.summary: BioWare veteran Mark Darrah has revealed an internal pitch for Dragon Age 4 that was never shared with fans.
articles.body:
BioWare veteran Mark Darrah has revealed an internal pitch for Dragon Age 4 that was never shared with fans.

This pitch was shared in the form of a book which Darrah says was distributed within BioWare and to higher ups at EA. The idea behind the book was to “remain relevant” with the publisher, and to try and secure early funding and new hires for the project.

“There's always a fear, and I think a legitimate fear, within a big publishing organization that you will get cancelled or in, the in case of EA, you will simply be allowed to be to remain on a starvation diet to the point where you cannot continue,” Darrah said in a new video published to his YouTube channel .

“This is where ultimately this book comes into being,” he continued. “This was made in mid-2016 to be something that I could give to the team, but also something I could give senior people within the EA organization to say, ‘Look, we're doing a Dragon Age. Don't forget that Dragon Age: Inquisition was a super great game that sold super well, so you want another one, right?’"

The book focusses on what was then referred to as Joplin, the original plan for a fourth Dragon Age game. This was later cancelled in favour of a live service Dragon Age 4, which in turn, was partially scrapped and retooled in the single-player Dragon Age: The Veilguard.

As for Joplin, this book gives us an idea as to what BioWare was cooking behind the scenes. For starters, we can see that there was a chapter on the game having a "reactive world." However, in The Veilguard, reactions to decisions made in previous games were almost entirely scrapped .

Darrah also shared that BioWare envisioned destructable environements, dynamic weather conditions, and social interactions that went beyond the standard BioWare conversations. There’s even a reference to the player taking part in heists, something we haven’t seen in the series before.

With that said, Darrah admitted that many of these features would have been scrapped even if development went well. In fact, BioWare was in the process of phasing out heists in 2017. But it does show us the vision BioWare was chasing, with a desire to make the series much more immersive than previous entries.

While Darrah failed to reveal the full content of the books, he did share the opening he wrote back in 2016:

“Dragon Age: Inquisition has transformed what the franchise is and how it is perceived by the public. As we move forward, we have a great opportunity to continue the breakout we have started.

“We stand upon the foundation laid by Dragon Age: Inquisition. A foundation that lets us see further. To see things that didn't work and fix them, to see things that did work and improve them.

“The Dragon Age team will create a more immersive interactive world with people in it who act and react like real people. We have a lot of work to do, but never has a Dragon Age game started in a stronger place. This document represents our current thinking on the next steps of the franchise.”

Needless to say, the developers did not get the development cycle they were hoping for. Instead, Joplin was scrapped, and Dragon Age stagnated to make way for Mass Effect: Andromeda and Anthem. The Dragon Age series was put on ice after The Veilguard failed to reach EA’s sales targets .

Now, BioWare has been shut down by EA. Many fans are fighting to save BioWare’s work, particularly the now-cancelled Mass Effect Universe, but we certainly shouldn’t expect any developments in the Dragon Age series anytime soon.

Rhiannon (she/her) is a freelance journalist who has been in the industry since 2019. She won MCV's Women in Games award in 2025 and adores RPGs. You can follow her on Bluesky at @rhithewitch.

articles.title: A Fellow Shepherd - Enshrouded Guide - IGN
articles.summary: A Fellow Shepherd is a main quest in Enshrouded from the Collector, who sends you out in search of a new Assistant for their research. You’ll have to
articles.body:
A Fellow Shepherd is a main quest in Enshrouded from the Collector, who sends you out in search of a new Assistant for their research. You’ll have to brake some of the Veilwater Basin’s toughest foes to find them, but the 400 XP makes the quest worth the while. This walkthrough will show you how to complete the quest so your Collector has some help around

For tips on how to have the best experience in Enshrouded, check out the following pages:

As long as you have the Collector unlocked, they’ll send you on this quest after you’ve activated the Ancient Spire in Veilwater Basin. Simply return to your base after you’ve done that and speak to them to start the quest.

To complete A Fellow Shepherd, you must travel to a Drak’Dal Temple far to the north in Veilwater Basin, in a high-level part of the region. The best way to get there is to glide north from the Ancient Spire and find the road that runs northeast from the Shrouded area near where you’ll land . That road will lead you through a Drak’Dal Camp and eventually to the Drak’Dal Ruin where you’ll find a bridge leading up to the temple.

When you reach the bridge, you’ll need to grapple twice across it to reach the foot of the temple. Drink your Drak Soulward Flask before you grapple across. You’ll encounter Level 43 Drak on the other side and that flask will help to even the odds.

Continue up the steps of the temple, and then down the stairs inside to descend into the Drak’s underground lair. When the stairs split, turn right and follow the corridor to find a grapple point you can use to cross the gap ahead.

Follow the next corridor and turn to your right at the end to find the first button for the temple’s door in a room at the end of the walkway.

Leave the room and hop down to the ledge below to find a Drak tablet you can read if you have the Drak Soulward Flask active.

Next, h op all the way down to the bottom level , and run around the walkway to find another small room with the next button.

On the opposite end of the walkway on the lower level, you’ll find a door. Open it and you’ll see two tracks with spike columns running back and forth along them. Time your approach so that you’re following one of them to the other end before side stepping it just before you reach the door.

Straight ahead from where you exit the spike column hallway, you’ll see a ledge with a gap and a room on the other side. Grapple across to that room to find the third and final button for the Drak’Dal Temple. The door you opened is back outside at the very top of the building, but don’t head to it just yet.

Open the door at the far end of the room where you found the third button and zig zag across the hallway to avoid the spike traps. At the other end, you’ll find Drak Relief V hanging on the wall. Pick it up and head back to the walkway you crossed after the spike column hallway.

How to Open the Secret Room in the Drak’Dal Temple

There’s a secret door in the Drak’Dal Temple with a line of inactive spike traps on the floor in front of it. To open the door, and claim the gold chest inside, you’ll have to find a hidden button within the hallway with two spike column traps .

The button is hidden inside a chamber you can only see through a hole in the wall at the middle of the hallway. Stop there, look through the hole and fire an arrow into it to unlock the secret door and claim its treasure.

With all the loot liberated from the Drak’Dal Temple, and the three buttons pressed, you can now wrap up the quest. Head back up and out of the temple and all the way up to the top to find the door you’ve opened. Inside is a Drak Chieftain who isn’t too keen on you showing up. His attack pattern should be familiar to you at this point; it’s similar to other sword-wielding Drak, but he deals a lot more damage. Fight defensively, parrying and avoiding attacks wherever possible to keep him from landing a blow and get in a few of your own.

Once the Chieftain is defeated, head into the room he was guarding and collect the soul from the skeleton on the table at the far end. You’ll complete the quest, earning you 400 XP and a new Assistant to summon into your settlement.

articles.title: James Gunn Shares Message to Fans Following Shock DC Studios Exit
articles.summary: Comic book movie maker James Gunn has shared a letter with fans after DC Studios announced he and Peter Safran would be stepping down as co-chairmen of DC Studios.
articles.body:
Comic book movie maker James Gunn has shared a letter with fans after DC Studios announced he and Peter Safran would be stepping down as co-chairmen of DC Studios.

'Shock' maybe doesn't do a good enough job of describing how DC movie watchers feel after the sudden shakeup was announced just moments ago. Although Gunn and Safran will remain creatively involved in at least some near-term projects, the plan is to see them vacate their positions starting December 1, leaving the future of the DCU slate uncertain as former Marvel exec Jeremy Latcham fills the role.

Gunn took to Threads to share thoughts on the matter in a lengthy statement. After four years in one of the most high-profile gigs in film and his role seemingly unaffected in the wake of the Paramount-Warner Bros. Skydance merger last month, it's safe to say no one was expecting to see him leave. But for Gunn, it was a long time coming.

"Oh, boy. What a four years," he began. "Thanks to all of you who have supported me and Peter in our time as the heads of DC Studios. When I was a kid growing up in Manchester, Missouri, I used to write and draw my own comics with a mix of DC Comics characters and my own characters. Having full access to these characters to do whatever we wanted has been a dream come true. I didn't know if I wanted this job when it was offered to me, but I just couldn't pass up the unique opportunity.

You don't have to look too hard to know that there are plenty of vocal people online who would disagree, but it's hard to argue that Gunn and Safran's oversight hasn't resulted in some success. The DCU lifted off with Superman just last year and was generally seen as a strong start for the budding universe. Supergirl arrived as an undeniable misstep this past June but was then followed by the praise brought forth by Lanterns . Clayface , which premiered just weeks ago, crossed $100 million this past weekend despite its relatively low budget and brutal body-horror concept.

These projects have their haters and lovers, but with Superman sequel Man of Tomorrow due out next year and The People v. Gorilla Grodd still in the works, there's no telling what will follow. Through the outside ups and downs, Gunn added that, behind the scenes, things have been tough.

9 DC Graphic Novels You Should Read to Understand James Gunn's DCU

"But what only the closest people to me have known over the past four years is my time at DC Studios has been trying, to say the least," he continued. "I dislike the at-times corporate nature of the job (thanks to Peter for taking the brunt of that). I'm always a very hard worker, but as a filmmaker, I would at least get to take short breaks to unwind, and I've stolen even that time from both myself and my loved one over the past four years (Jenn [Jennifer Holland], I love you and I'm sorry, and you don't need to feel guilty for being the happiest of all people that I'm no longer doing this job). And the thing my ADHD hyperfocus has had the most difficulty with has been dividing my time between projects I'm incredibly passionate about and the ones I'm not so much and all the things I have to do as a studio head.

"There have been so many highs along the way – releasing Superman and Clayface, making Peacemaker, reading the scripts to [The People v. Gorilla Grodd], the entire process of Man of Tomorrow, which thus far has been the best filmmaking experience of my life, and numerous other moments.

"The highest of the highs have been all the talented and wonderful people I've worked with and grown to love: the DC Studios crew, our talented collaborators, our casts and crews, and the boisterous and hilarious fans. And the best part of all has been working with Peter Safra, the smartest and most competent person I know. You've been the best partner a person could ask for, and, more so, a truly good friend.

Gunn signed off: "So, yes, I will miss the people around me, and I will miss being the co-caretaker of these great characters, but I'm also incredibly relieved and excited to get back to pure filmmaking.

"That's not to say Peter and I are immediately done with DC or superheroes. We have Man of Tomorrow out this summer. And we've just been engaged on another DC project which I'm writing, and we'll see where it goes after that. And, of course, the characters we set up will live on.

"Thank you so very, very much for embracing the characters and stories we've put on screen. Love and gratitude, James Gunn."

James Gunn's Man of Tomorrow: Superman vs. Lex Luthor Art Gallery

Gunn and Safran's exit from DC Studios is still very, very fresh, so we won't have a clear picture of how it might affect the DCU for quite some time. The exact details behind the shakeup are also unclear.

While the DCU has brought a few Green Lanterns, Clark Kent, and more iconic superheroes into the live-action realm, there are plenty of other question marks left hanging. Despite rumors , there's been no official sign of Wonder Woman, and DC Studios has continued to keep fans in the dark when it comes to the next new Batman. Meanwhile, regardless of any shuffling behind the scenes, The Batman Part 2 is still roaring toward its February 18, 2028, release date.

You can see the full list of every DC project in the works as of right now . With new leadership stepping in, expect big changes as soon as December. What's next for Gunn and Safran after their creative work wraps up remains to be seen.

IGN caught up with Gunn's comic book movie partner for an interview last month. For more, you can read what Gunn had to say about the DCU's approach to an interconnected movie universe .

Photo by Stewart Cook/Warner Bros. via Getty Images.

Michael Cripe is a freelance writer with IGN. He's best known for his work at sites like The Pitch, The Escapist, and OnlySP. Be sure to give him a follow on Bluesky (@mikecripe.bsky.social) and Twitter (@MikeCripe).

articles.title: Disaster in Goron City Walkthrough - The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Welcome to IGN's Guide to The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake. After 28 years, Ocarina of Time has been fully remade, and while much of it remains
articles.body:
Welcome to IGN's Guide to The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake. After 28 years, Ocarina of Time has been fully remade, and while much of it remains the same, there's plenty of new differences to be found while exploring Hyrule. Now that the Forest Temple has been cleansed and the Sage of the Forest awakened, Link must search Death Mountain to find the next Sage, but will need the help of the Goron Tunic to survive the volcano's extreme heat.

It's been seven years since Link last visited the Gorons of Death Mountain, and the ominous looking volcano on the horizon seems more dangerous than ever. Armed with your new Hookshot and Fairy Bow, it's time to pay your Sworn Brother a visit!

While the ascent up the Death Mountain Trail is just as short as ever, it has grown more dangerous since last you were here. The Tektites might not be so threatening anymore, but the stream of deadly boulders rolling down the mountain are a deadly new addition!

Hug the right side of the trail once a boulder passes to slip around, and use the alcoves as cover until you reach the first ledge and a bit of a respite. There are new large grey rock chunks everywhere, but your bombs lack the ability to break them apart.

Did you remember to plant those Magic Beans in the soil outside of the entrance to Dodongo Cavern all those years ago? If you did, you can now ride up using the new floating magic plant to finally reach the high ledge above holding the Piece of Heart that's been taunting you for so long!

Speaking of Dodongo Cavern, it's the only dungeon from your childhood you can still enter, and there's actually a reason for that. Head back inside, moving through the entrance hall and taking the first hallway path to the east. You may remember there was a high ledge above the Baby Dodongos you couldn't reach before, but now there's a gust of straw coming up from that spot. If you made an official Scarecrow Song for Bonooru and Pierre, play it here, and Pierre will appear. This allows you to hookshot up to him, where you'll find the dungeon's last Gold Skulltula!

Continue up the mountain trail, dodging the next train of boulders rolling down from the trail to the summit by sticking to the left wall until you can enter the tunnel path toward Goron City. The old Bomb Flower and its attendant are gone, as are pretty much all the Gorons that used to be out on the trail.

One thing you can uncover is a Grotto entrance over on the right side before the city entrance, and play the Song of Storms to make the propeller plant disappear. Inside, you'll find a fog-filled cavern room with several Baby Dodongos hiding beneath the mist. Defeat them, and help yourself to all the Rupees down here!

Unlike Kokiri Forest, Goron City has not been overrun by monsters, thankfully. And yet, it seems pretty quiet here now. Where is everyone? To answer, a young Goron will spy you entering, and start rolling away in fear that you're here to do no good.

He'll roll around the city layer just one ring below the main entrance, and moves pretty fast, daring you to stop him. Like the other Goron in the city when you were a child, you'll need to stun him with a well-timed exploding bomb to get him to stop his endless rolling.

The good news is you don't have to waste your precious bombs: look to the right of the entrance to spot a group of Bomb Flowers by one of the rope bridges leading to the central platform the Spiritual Stone used to be on. From here, you'll have a good vantage point to spot him rolling from afar.

If you're having trouble judging the distance, you can try dropping down first to startle him and make him roll clockwise, so his approach isn't obscured by the tunnel. Making him turn around and roll the other way also slows him down, so you can force him to stop when rolling past a bomb to ensure he gets stunned by the blast!

Once the Goron kid is seeing stars, move over to talk to... Link? Apparently this kid was named by his father Darunia after your Dodongo-slaying exploits! From the little Goron, you'll learn that Ganondorf came and kidnapped all of the Gorons, taking them to the Fire Temple to be sacrificed to an ancient dragon. Darunia seems to have gone to the temple to help, but no one has returned.

Talk to the kid to try cheering him up, and when Link offers to save the day, you'll get a special thank you present: The Goron Tunic! With this fashionable red tunic, you'll be able to survive the extreme heat of Death Mountain's crater!

The little Goron Link will open up access to the rest of the city for you, including a secret path to the crater behind the statue in Darunia's Chambers.

Before you head off, there's a few things you can do around here:

Back on the top floor, head to the east side to find Medigoron's room. Apparently he was too big to kidnap so Ganondorf just kind of left him there. The sword he's been working on since you were a child is finally ready to buy, now that you're an adult. It's called the Giant's Knife, and though strong, he'll also caution its pretty brittle. If you want to give it a try, it's 200 Rupees to buy one, just be warned that after a bit of attacking the blade will snap, which will both drastically reduce the blade's reach and damage output. But... it does look kind of cool.

If you're hoping for something a bit more resilient, there is a way to get something more durable, but we lack the tools to procure one right now.

Head back down to the floor below where you met up with Goron Link, and move around to the north side. This should put you around the tunnel on the opposite side of the high platform where the Spiritual Stone used to rest. Jutting out below the platform is a rocky outcropping, where a Gold Skulltula can be found.

Be sure to also look for a small tunnel entrance on the southwest side on this level. It leads to a long lava-filled room you can spot on the mini-map. Though you were unable to traverse this area as a kid, you can now use the Hookshot to zip over the lava to the far side, leading to a Grotto.

Inside, you'll be presented with a puzzle: a sign will notify you that the five other signs have explicit instructions on which signs need to be cut. Cut the wrong ones, and you won't get the good prize (If you bought the Giant's Knife, swap to the Master Sword so you don't accidentally slash signs with its big range). From left to right:

The First Sign says "Cut this if there are no other signs to cut". This will be the last sign you cut.

The Second Sign says "Don't Cut this." Do not cut this sign.

The Third Sign says "You can cut this right away." Cut this sign.

The Fourth Sign says "Maybe you can cut this. Maybe not." Do no cut this sign.

The Fifth Sign says "You can cut this, but you can't cut the left one." Cut this sign.

After cutting 3 and 5, cut Sign 1 last, and if you were correct, a Treasure Chest to the right will appear, holding a Purple Rupee!

You can check out the Goron Shop near Darunia's Chambers if you want (the only other Goron that escaped being kidnapped. He also sells a Goron Tunic, which is good to remember if for some reason you lose the one you were given.

To reach the secret path, enter Darunia's Chambers can look for the large statue at the back of the room. Pull it outward, and you'll find a hidden path beyond.

Be sure to equip your Goron Tunic as you enter! If not, you'll steadily take damage from the extreme heat, which is very inadvisable!

There's a side path to the southwest leading back up to the summit of the crater, but large grey rocks block you from that pathway. Instead, use the Hookshot to zip across the broken bridge to the east.

It's here you'll meet Sheik (who must be rocking a Goron Tunic under their ninja garb). Just like at the entrance to the Forest Temple, the Sheikah warrior will have a new melody for you to play:

Complete this prompt to learn the Bolero of Fire, allowing you to return to the fiery crater of Death Mountain whenever you wish!

After Sheik makes another dramatic entrance, there's a few things left to do before going inside. If you didn't explore the summit as a child, it's worth going back to get two Heart Pieces and a Gold Skulltula when you can. And if you look near the large platform by the temple entrance, you can find a long abandoned patch of soft soil.

Warp back to the Temple of Time, head to Zora River, and grab another helping of Magic Beans and a bottled Bug. Play the new Bolero of Fire to teleport over to the Fire Temple. Even though Link cant enter as a child, you can quickly plant some Magic Beans nearby, and drop a Bug into the soil to produce a Gold Skulltula (just be quick since you'll be on fire the whole time)!

With the Magic Beans planted in Death Mountain Crater in the past, return to the adult timeline, and warp back outside the Fire Temple. The now ripened magic plant seems to be doing just fine in the heat, and you can step on it to float all around the crater. This allows you to get the other Heart Piece if you missed it, as well as a brand new Piece of Heart on top of one of the large rocky pillars in the crater!

Note that if you're looking for some extra money, there's a low platform on the lava east of the temple entrance. From here, you can spot a higher platform with a gust of straw. Play the Scarecrow's Song and watch out for ambushing enemies as you make your way across to the far side.

At the end, there's a broken bridge up to the right, and another spot to play the Scarecrow's Song once more. Zip up again to the high ledge, and you'll find a ring of Rupees around a Purple Rupee!

Once you're all stocked on gear and supplies, head north to enter the Fire Temple .

articles.body:
Batman fans are eating… well, bad. Or not much at all. We’re actually starving. Across both video games and movies.

You’ve no doubt seen today’s shocking news that DCU bosses James Gunn and Peter Safran are out at Warner Br… er, Skydance. And thus, the DCU Batman might not even happen. Or rather, there definitely will be a new big-screen Batman eventually, but Gunn’s entire DCU plan may very well be out the window and we might be starting over. Again. Sigh…

Batman has always been my favorite superhero, and so today’s Gunn news has been bumming me out a little more than expected, because I realized that when you account for what’s going on with the Dark Knight in games and movies – or maybe more specifically, what’s not going on, it’s time to accept that we’re in a proper Batman drought.

To zoom out on the movies for a moment, the last time we saw Batman on the big screen was four years ago, via Matt Reeves’s brilliant Robert Pattinson-led The Batman. Prior to that, the Caped Crusader showed up in live-action form in The Snyder Cut of Justice League in 2021 – though obviously that was a movie we’d mostly already seen. And it was a superhero ensemble. With apologies to Batman vs. Superman, where Batfleck had to share the screen with Henry Cavill (though I will always appreciate it solely for the warehouse scene, which is my favorite Batman fight scene ever), you have to go all the way back to Christopher Nolan’s The Dark Knight Rises in 2012 for the last proper live-action Batman film before Matt Reeves’s 2022 gem. Fortunately, DC Animated Studios continues to look out for us Bat-fans, most recently with the stellar Batman: Knightfall Part 1, with an honorable mention to Amazon's really good Batman: Caped Crusader series.

At least we’ve got The Batman Part 2 to look forward to in 2028 … right? Skydance wouldn’t dare pull the plug on it, would they? <insert nervous laughter here>

Batman fans looking for solace in video games arguably have it even worse. Because remember, Gunn was in charge of games, too . Technically, the most recent Batman game was the perfectly good VR entry in the Arkham series, Batman: Arkham Shadow in 2024. But let’s be honest: not a lot of people played that because VR continues to be a chicken-and-egg technology that remains frustratingly far from the mainstream – though I give Meta a lot of credit for trying to get people to invest in VR by producing games like Arkham Shadow.

Speaking of the Batman Arkham games, it has now been a full decade since the last mainline entry, Arkham Knight. Yes, you read that right: 10 years have gone by since Rocksteady completed its incredible trilogy that rewrote the rules – and the expectations – for both Batman games and, dare I say, superhero games in general. It hasn’t been pretty since then, though this next part definitely isn’t Skydance’s fault.

Rocksteady, presumably by order of someone in the Warner Bros. C-suite who saw the live-service craze taking off on the back of Bungie’s Destiny games, got work not on a new Batman game, but instead on a Suicide Squad multiplayer live-service game. It was plain to see ahead of time that it wasn’t going to go well , and surprise surprise, it didn’t . The result has been a wounded studio that, sadly all too predictably, suffered layoffs . And before Suicide Squad even shipped, Rocksteady cofounders Sefton Hill and Jaime Walker, perhaps seeing the writing on the wall, left and started a new team , taking some number of Rocksteady developers with them.

The good news is that Rocksteady is reportedly at work on a new single-player Batman game, but it’s likely many years away as the studio picks up the pieces broken by Suicide Squad. The bad news is, even that game’s existence is fair to call into question after Paramount’s acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery . The upstart Paramount Games was merged with WB Games, of which Rocksteady was a part. And, in another woefully unsurprising move, that group just got hit with layoffs.

So where does that leave Rocksteady? We’re not sure yet. Where does that leave Batman video games? Well, unless WB Games had already been wise enough to go the Lucasfilm route of licensing its properties out to talented external developers prior to Paramount/Skydance entering the picture, the wait for a proper new AAA Batman game for PC and consoles might go on for a lot longer. Sure, Traveller’s Tales cooked with Lego Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight, but that game is to the main Arkham games as the animated Batman: Knightfall is to The Batman Part 2, meaning “it’s cool, but not the big thing everyone eagerly wants and anticipates.”

Here’s hoping Skydance has a plan for Batman that it’s willing to stick to – even if it’s Gunn’s plan. It’s already been way too long for one of the most popular superheroes on Earth to have sat on the sidelines on both consoles and the big screen. Let’s hope DC’s progress doesn’t get reset to zero. Again.

Now if you’ll excuse me, I’m going to go rewatch The Batman for the 50th time, The Dark Knight for the thousandth time, and replay the Arkham trilogy for the umpteenth time.
